Subordinate all other resources to the constraint's pace
Repeat the process on a different resource
Exploit the constraint — extract maximum output from it as-is before spending capital
content.stem: Under the theory of constraints, immediately after IDENTIFYING the system's bottleneck, the next step per the five focusing steps is to:
content.why: TOC's five steps: identify → exploit → subordinate → elevate → repeat. Exploiting (squeezing maximum output from existing capacity — no lost minutes, quality-checked feed) comes before subordinating other resources and before spending capital to elevate.

options: Publishing more accurate daily production schedules
Authorizing upstream production only when a downstream kanban signals actual consumption
Adding more WIP buffer ahead of the bottleneck
content.stem: A team converts a push production system to pull on a finishing floor. The essential change that accomplishes this is:
content.why: Pull means downstream consumption authorizes upstream work via a kanban signal, with WIP capped by card count. Better forecasts or schedules still push material regardless of actual downstream need — that remains a push system.

content.stem: Operators walk 40 meters each cycle to retrieve test rings from a central rack. In the eight-wastes taxonomy (DOWNTIME), this is classified as:
content.why: Motion is unnecessary movement of people; transportation is movement of material/product. This distinction — what is actually moving — is frequently tested.

options: Increased variation from overadjustment (tampering) — reacting to common cause as if it were special cause
content.stem: A control chart shows a stable, in-control process, but an operator adjusts machine settings after every point that deviates from the target centerline. Per Deming's funnel experiment, the predictable result is:
content.why: Adjusting in response to common-cause variation is tampering — Deming's funnel experiment rule 2 shows this roughly doubles variance. Control charts exist to distinguish signals worth acting on from noise that should be left alone.

options: IV — main effects are clear of two-factor interactions, but two-factor interactions alias each other
content.stem: A DOE screening design with 4 factors at 2 levels using only 8 runs (2⁴⁻¹, generator I=ABCD) has resolution:
content.why: The shortest word in the defining relation has length 4 → Resolution IV. Main effects are clear of 2FIs, but 2FIs alias with each other (e.g., AB=CD). Resolution equals the length of the shortest defining word — a directly testable rule.

A rule that cost is the only consequence considered

They also noticed an increase in customers after this change. Which of the following improvement methods does this scenario describe?
content.why: Reengineering a process involves a complete and radical redesign of a procedure. In this case, the restaurant has completely redesigned its kitchen and ordering procedure to achieve large improvements in its serving time and sales— an example of reengineering. [V.C]

content.stem: What value of Cp is associated with a Six Sigma–quality level process?
content.why: The capability index is Cp = (USL - LSL)/(6σ). A Six Sigma quality level places the specifications 12σ apart, so Cp = 12σ/(6σ) = 2.0. [V.C]

content.stem: A project is being conducted in a hospital clinic. Which of the following are considered continuous data?
content.why: Discrete data can only take on countable values. The result of the medical test is pass/fail. Errors in the medical record and the number of patient falls have possible values of 0, 1, 2, . . . . Patient weight can be an infinite number of values and is therefore continuous data. [VI.A.1]

content.stem: A project is being conducted in a manufacturing facility. Which of the following are considered discrete data?
content.why: Length, volume, and time can take on values over an interval of numbers. There are infinitely many values between any two values on their respective scales. Number of nonconforming components, however, can only take on a set of countable values, so it is discrete data. [VI.A.1]

content.stem: Which of the following can simplify recording and analysis of data?
content.why: Coding data can simplify recording and analysis. Sometimes it is useful to code data using an algebraic transformation. Suppose a set of data has mean μ and standard deviation σ. A new data set may be created using the formula y = ax + b. Each element of the new set is formed by multiplying an element of the original set by a, then adding b. [VI.A.3]

content.stem: The waiting times in minutes for eight customers at a bank are: 5, 8, 12, 3, 2, 7, 6, 5. What are the mean and median for this sample of waiting times?
content.why: The mean is (5 + 8 + 12 + 3 + 2 + 7 + 6 + 5)/8 = 6 minutes. Ordered data are 2, 3, 5, 5, 6, 7, 8, 12, so the median is (5 + 6)/2 = 5.5 minutes. [VI.A.6]

content.stem: The lengths in inches for a sample of seven components are: 3.2, 3.1, 3.4, 3.1, 3.2, 3.3, 3.2. What is the standard deviation for this sample?
content.why: The sample mean is x̄ = 22.5/7 = 3.2143. Using s = √[Σ(xi-x̄)²/(n-1)] gives s = 0.1069 inches. [VI.A.6]

content.stem: The median of a population is much larger than the population mean. What can you say about the shape of the population distribution?
content.why: The population mean and median are not equal, so the distribution cannot be symmetric. The mean is sensitive to the data, while the median is a robust statistic and is not heavily influenced by extreme observations. Therefore, a much smaller mean indicates that the data are skewed to the left. [VI.A.5]

content.stem: A population has an exponential distribution. One hundred samples of size 40 are randomly collected and the 100 sample means are calculated. What is the approximate distribution of these sample averages?
content.why: Under the central limit theorem, the distribution of sample averages tends toward a normal distribution as the sample size increases. Although the exponential distribution is right skewed, the distribution of sample averages is approximately normally distributed for large sample sizes. In this case n = 40. [VI.A.6]

content.stem: What is the formula for the population variance?
content.why: Population variance is the average squared deviation from the population mean: σ² = (1/N)Σi=1N(xi-μ)². The denominator N distinguishes it from the usual sample-variance formula. [VI.A.6]

content.stem: A team would like to compare waiting times of customers by day of the week. Which of the following would be the most appropriate tool to use?
content.why: Side-by-side box plots can be used to easily compare any differences between the wait times by day of the week. Histograms are more suited for describing the distribution of one population. Scatter plots are used to examine the relationship between two continuous variables. Probability plots are used to determine whether data follow a certain distribution, for example, the normal distribution. [VI.A.7]

content.stem: The temperature of coffee is an important characteristic in a restaurant. The temperature of fifteen randomly selected cups of coffee is measured and the average temperature is found to be 168°F. Which term best describes this average temperature?
content.why: The average temperature of fifteen randomly selected cups of coffee is a statistic. A statistic is a characteristic of a sample and is used to estimate the population parameter. In this case, the sample mean temperature of the fifteen cups of coffee can be used to estimate the temperature of all coffee served in the restaurant. [VI.B.1]

content.stem: Business processes, customers, and financial fundamentals are all perspectives of what philosophy?
content.why: Business processes, customers, and financial fundamentals are part of the balanced scorecard, with the other category being learning and growth. [I.B.2.b]

content.stem: A characteristic of a population is called a:
content.why: A parameter is a characteristic of a population. It is a quantity that describes characteristics of a population. The value of a population parameter is frequently unknown and must be estimated by a sample statistic. [VI.B.1]

content.stem: The probability of a part being defective is 0.02. What is the probability it is not defective?
content.why: Use the complement rule: P(not defective) = 1 - P(defective) = 1 - 0.02 = 0.98. [VI.B.3]

content.stem: The probability that event A occurs is 0.72. The probability that event B occurs is 0.03. What is the probability that events A and B both occur?
content.why: There is not enough information provided to determine the probability that both events A and B occur. If it were stated that A and B were independent, then the multiplication rule would apply: P(A ∩ B) = P(A) × P(B). [VI.B.3]

content.stem: If the probability that event A occurs is 0.40, the probability that event B occurs is 0.13, and A and B are mutually exclusive events, what is the probability that events A and B both occur?
content.why: Since events A and B are mutually exclusive, they cannot occur simultaneously. Therefore, P(A ∩ B) = 0. Note that P(A ∪ B) = P(A) + P(B) = 0.40 + 0.13 = 0.53, since A and B are mutually exclusive. Recall that probabilities only take on values between 0 and 1. [VI.B.3]

content.stem: The time between arrivals at a store has an exponential distribution with mean five minutes. What is the probability that the time between arrivals is less than three minutes?
content.why: The exponential rate is λ = 1/5 = 0.2 per minute. Therefore, P(T < 3) = 1 - e-0.2(3) = 1 - e-0.6 = 0.4512. [VI.C.1]

Which of the following probability distributions is asymmetric?
content.why: The normal distribution, t-distribution, and uniform distribution are all symmetric probability distributions. Asymmetric distributions include the exponential distribution, Weibull distribution, chi-square distribution, and lognormal distribution. [VI.C.1]

content.stem: A bottling company’s filling process has a normal distribution with mean 24.01 oz. and standard deviation 0.025 oz. If the specifications for the process are 24 ± .08 oz, what proportion of bottles is overfilled?
content.why: The upper specification limit is 24.08 oz. Standardizing gives z = (24.08 - 24.01)/0.025 = 2.80. Therefore, P(X > 24.08) = P(Z > 2.80) = 0.00256. [VI.C.1]

content.why: The hypergeometric distribution is appropriate when the sample is taken without replacement from a finite population. content.stem: Fifteen invoices are randomly selected from a batch at a company. It is believed that 10% of all invoices have an error. What is the probability that exactly four out of the fifteen invoices have an error?
content.why: This is binomial with n = 15 and p = 0.10. P(X=4) = C(15,4)(0.10)⁴(0.90)¹¹ = 0.0428. [VI.C.2]

content.stem: A population has a distribution with mean 24 and standard deviation 5.5. According to the central limit theorem, what is the mean of the distribution of the sample means for random samples of size 32?
content.why: The central limit theorem states that if the sample size n is sufficiently large, then the sample mean X– follows approximately a normal distribution with mean µX– = µ and standard deviation σX– =σ/ .n In this case, µ = 24, σ = 5.5, and n = 32. Therefore, µX– = µ = 24. [VI.C.2]

content.stem: A bottling company’s filling process has a normal distribution with mean 24 oz. and standard deviation 0.05 oz. What is the probability that a sample of sixteen randomly selected bottles will have an average volume more than 24.04 oz?
A sample of size 16 is drawn from a population that follows a normal distribution with mean 58 and variance 64. What is the standard error of the sample mean?
content.why: The population standard deviation is σ = √64 = 8. The standard error is σ/√n = 8/√16 = 2. [VI.D.1]

content.why: Recall that the true value of the population proportion is unknown. Answer (d) describes the practical interpretation of the confidence interval: with 95% confidence, the population proportion will lie between 0.02 and 0.12. [VI.D.1]

content.stem: A team would like to estimate the average length of a component. A random sample of 50 components had a sample mean of 11.75 mm. Which of the following terms is used to describe this value?
content.why: 11.73 mm is a point estimate for the average length of the component. Recall that a parameter is a characteristic of a population. The sample mean is often a point estimator for the population mean. [VI.D.1]

content.stem: The tensile strength of fifteen units of cement was tested. The sample mean tensile strength was 4.3 MPa and sample standard deviation was 0.51 MPa. Find a 99% confidence interval for the true mean tensile strength of the cement.
content.why: Because σ is unknown and n = 15, use a t interval with 14 degrees of freedom. With t0.005,14 = 2.977, the interval is 4.3 ± 2.977(0.51/√15) = (3.908, 4.692) MPa. [VI.D.1]

content.stem: A team would like to estimate the true average tensile strength of cement. They would like to obtain an estimate within 0.15 MPa of the true average tensile strength with 95% confidence. Based on prior information, it is assumed that σ = 0.50 MPa. What sample size is required to meet these requirements?
content.why: For margin of error E = 0.15 with 95% confidence, n = (z0.025σ/E)² = (1.96 × 0.50/0.15)² = 42.68. Round up to 43. [VI.D.1]

content.stem: The voltage of a power supply is of interest to a team. Voltage is assumed to be normally distributed. The voltages of seven randomly selected observations are: 10.37, 11.50, 9.80, 10.65, 11.95, 10.15, 9.52. Find the 95% confidence interval on the population variance of voltage.
content.why: For normally distributed data, the 95% confidence interval for the population variance is ((n-1)s²/χ²₀.₉₇₅, (n-1)s²/χ²₀.₀₂₅). With n = 7 and s² = 0.781, the interval is approximately (0.324, 3.788). [VI.D.1]

content.stem: According to ISO 9001:2015, what enables an organization to determine the factors that could cause its processes and its quality management system to deviate from planned results, to put in place preventive controls to minimize negative effects, and to make maximum use of opportunities as they arise?
content.why: These are elements of risk-based thinking per ISO 9001:2015, clause 0.1. Risk culture is the way of thinking informed by a set of organizational values that determine behavior in face of uncertainty; specifically, the decision making regarding routine and nonroutine risk confrontation and associated risk identification, analysis, evaluation, monitoring, modification and communication. A risk register is a log of assessed and identified risks. FMEA is a form of risk register. [VII.A.1]

content.stem: Carrying out preventive action to eliminate potential nonconformities, analyzing any nonconformities that do occur, and taking action to prevent recurrence that is appropriate for the effects of the nonconformity are examples of:

Fault tree analysis is a tool to identify failures or faults that can lead to a top- level failure event. Hazard analysis is a process to analyze the hazards and their consequences related to product or process under study. Vendor risk oversight involves the vendor or supplier, which is not mentioned here. [VII.A.1]

content.stem: A baby is playing near a glass bottle of pesticide. In this situation, what is the bottle of pesticide?
content.why: A hazard is a potential source of harm or a potential condition that, through a sequence of events, can cause a consequence. A harm is a physical or physiological damage, which here has not been realized yet. Risk here would include scenarios (and their severity and probability) such as the child toppling the bottle or contacting the pesticide. Consequence is the measure of impact – none of which have occurred yet. To classify negative impacts, the term severity is commonly used. [VII.A.1]

options: should include only risks that it has control over.
should include only those risks that are obvious and currently known.
should include all possible risks, using many risk identification tools.
should only come up with a list of no more than three to five risks or hazards.
content.stem: Risk identification is the process of identifying hazards and sources of risks. When an organization is determining possible risks it:
content.why: The purpose of risk identification is to identify all possible risks whether current, possible future risks, risks that are not currently under the organization’s control, or risks that may occur due to results of an accumulation of factors or steps in the process. [VII.A.1]

content.stem: The key stakeholders, strategy, and program objectives, as well as development of roles and responsibilities, are typically identified and agreed on in the:
content.why: The planning phase is important for setting all ground rules and objectives, and identifying key stakeholders. It may also include selecting key documents and templates for risk analysis. [VII.A.1]

options: make decisions based on risk level compared to stated risk criteria.
decide whether risk levels are acceptable.
evaluate and possibly change the consequences.
content.stem: In a risk analysis, the likelihood and consequences of risk are combined to determine the risk level for a particular risk. The purpose of risk evaluation is to:
content.why: Risk evaluation is used to make decisions about which risks need to be addressed based on the estimate of metrics identified in risk analysis—combined results of the likelihood of the risk and the consequences. [VII.A.1]

content.stem: The rate of aviation fatalities in 1970 was 6.35 per million flights; in 2017, it was 0.39. Which of the following would a company today be failing to understand if it still considered the 1970 rate acceptable?
content.why: External context is the environment within which the organization seeks to achieve its objectives. The industry benchmark changed between 1970 and 2017 . Cultural context is incorrect and is the environment or situation that is relevant to the beliefs, values, and practices of the culture under study. [VII.A.2]

content.stem: Assessment of organizational objectives and paths to their achievement, prevention of undesired outcomes, and continuous improvement are all goals of:
content.why: Risk management promotes continuous improvement and desired outcomes at the organizational level. The other options may contribute, but risk management provides the overarching umbrella. [VII.B.1]

options: No, because compliant organizational processes must be followed
Yes, because it doesn’t make sense to revise the documents
No, because risk-based thinking begins with the requirements gathering stage
Yes, because risk control measures can best be meaningfully implemented in the later stages
content.stem: As a Quality Manager for new products introduction, the design manager requests that you produce all risk documentation after the design is finalized and frozen to avoid redundant work. Would you follow his recommendation and why?
content.why: It is important to not wait for the final design freeze, but to perform preliminary risk analysis early on. The closer to the requirements-gathering phase the risk analysis is performed, the easier and less expensive it will be to implement risk modification measures. The concept of risk-based thinking is to have not only the designers thinking about potential hazards and their consequences from the first stroke of their pencils but also for the process owners and the finance, marketing, clinical, engineering, operations, and other relevant functions thinking the same way. [VII.B.1]

options: express the value of present-day dollars as some projected future value.
express future costs and benefits in present-day dollars.
know what interest rates in the future will be.
know the lifecycle of the product or project being considered.
content.stem: To consider the costs and benefits of a future project it is necessary to:
content.why: In cost-benefit analysis, the financial analysis is performed based on translations to today’s value. [I.B.2.c]

content.stem: Results of risk evaluation must be:
content.why: Once a risk analysis has been performed, the final evaluation of the results may be quantitative or qualitative, or both. [VII.B.2]

content.stem: Which of the following is a phase of the risk assessment process per ISO 31000:2018?
content.why: ISO 31000:2018 divides the risk assessment process into three distinct and sequential phases: risk identification, risk analysis, and risk evaluation. At all levels of risk management, risk assessment is an activating phase that is critical to the risk management process and will require significant resources. [VII.B.2]

content.stem: Reconsidering objectives and doing nothing are decisions that can be taken after:
content.why: The process of risk evaluation is performed by comparing the estimated risk against the baseline criteria to determine the risk acceptability. It is the exercise of assessing action for estimated risks based on their respective significance to the objectives in terms of concerned product, service, process, or business. ISO 31000:2018 states: ”Risk evaluation involves comparing the results of the risk analysis with the established risk criteria to determine where additional action is required. This can lead to a decision to: do nothing further; consider risk treatment options; undertake further analysis to better understand the risk; maintain existing controls; reconsider objectives.” [VII.B.2]

content.stem: The process of comparing the results of a risk analysis that has been completed to the stated risk criteria put in place is:
content.why: Risk evaluation; once estimates of the evaluation metrics have been calculated, they should be compared to the level of risk or risk criteria already in place to determine whether the level of risk is acceptable. [VII.B.2]

options: risk reduction, risk criteria, and evaluation.
content.stem: Risk assessment consists of the following:
content.why: The three components of risk assessment are risk identification, risk analysis, and risk evaluation. [VII.B.2]

content.stem: A risk assessment tool that is based on expert opinion is the:
content.why: The Delphi method is based on the idea that group decisions or judgments will be more accurate than those of individuals. [VII.B.2]

options: it cannot be used to identify combinations of failure modes, only single failure modes.
it does not aid in identifying possible root causes.
it is too complicated since it does not require the user to know anything about the process or product.
it cannot be used to prioritize risks.
content.stem: One of the drawbacks or limitations of the FMEA is that:
content.why: The FMEA cannot identify combinations of failure modes, and failure mode combinations may be significant. [VII.B.2]

content.stem: Two components of risk estimation are:
content.why: The two components for risk estimation include the probability of occurrence of harm and the severity or potential harm. [VII.B.2]

content.stem: Qualitative evaluation involves categories such as catastrophic, critical, major, minor, and negligible, which represent:
content.why: The qualitative assessment where the degree of risk or harm is given as catastrophic, critical, and so on, represents the severity or potential harm. [VII.B.2]

content.stem: The numerical metric that is an output from an FMEA is the:
content.why: The risk priority number is a numerical result from the FMEA. The RPN is the result of multiplying three values: severity of failure, failure likelihood, and the likelihood of detecting the failure. [VII.B.2]

content.stem: In a RACI Matrix, the letters RACI stand for:
content.why: RACI stand for Responsible, Accountable, Consulted, Informed. [I.B.2.d] 17 . b; The Accountable person is ultimately answerable for the successful completion of the task, so there can be only one person where “the buck stops here.” [I.B.2.d]

options: Failure mode and effects criticality analysis (FMECA)
content.stem: Which of the following risk assessment tools is a top-down approach to failure mode analysis?
content.why: FMEA and FMECA are both bottom-up approaches, while FTA is a top-down approach. [VII.B.2]

content.stem: When assessing Audit nonconformities as an Auditor, it is recommended to use a(n):
content.why: According to The ASQ Certified Quality Engineer Handbook, Fifth Edition, when assessing audit nonconformities, it is recommended to use a risk-based approach. Delineating between a major and minor nonconformance should be based on the level of risk and the analysis of audit objective evidence. [II.D.3]

options: the auditee, auditor, and closing meeting.
the management review meeting, final inspection, and design reviews.
the audit scope, depth, and time frame.
the ISO certification body audit, FDA inspection, and OSHA audit.
content.stem: Audit planning by the lead Auditor should include consideration of:
content.why: Proper planning is a key factor in achieving an efficient quality audit. Planning should be conducted with consideration of the client expectations, which include the scope, depth, and time frame. The lead auditor is responsible for planning and conducting the audit. [II.D.3]

options: should be agreed on by all parties: client, auditor, auditee.
is conducted by someone in the company when there is time.
is communicated via memo from the auditee.
content.stem: The auditee will begin improvement efforts to address any problems or corrections identified by the audit. A follow-up audit to verify results of this improvement effort:
content.why: A follow-up audit is necessary to determine whether the problems and recommended corrections have been addressed. All three parties should arrange and agree on a follow-up audit. [II.D.4]

content.stem: A company increased prevention costs by making changes to its quality control area, and then nonconformities decreased. As a result, there was a reduction in:
content.why: An increase in prevention costs, resulting in a decrease in defects and nonconformities, will result in a decrease in failure costs due to the reduction of defects and nonconformities. [II.E]

content.stem: Correction of data entry errors, specimen processing, and cost of reeducating staff in a laboratory before delivery of the results to the customer are examples of:
content.why: Since the data error correction, reprocessing, and reeducation occur before delivery of the product or service, the cost incurred would be an internal failure cost. [II.E]

content.stem: In one year, the cost of proficiency testing for quality assurance inspectors by an external certified agency for all employees was $10,000. This cost would be categorized as:
content.why: Costs associated with activities performed to uncover or identify deficiencies, such as in personnel proficiency, are considered appraisal costs. [II.E]

content.stem: Money spent on review of suppliers is:
content.why: Costs associated with activities related to supplier reviews are known as prevention costs. [II.E]

options: There is no relationship between the two.
Appraisal activities will remain the same.
content.stem: As failure costs decrease due to improved quality, what typically happens to appraisal activities?
content.why: As failures are uncovered and corrected, appraisal activities will generally decrease, although appraisal activities will not and should not be completely eliminated. The type of appraisal activity can change. [II.E]

content.stem: Test equipment depreciation is an example of:
content.why: Depreciation of test equipment is a cost associated with measuring products to ensure conformance with quality standards and performance requirements, so it is an appraisal cost. [II.E]

options: Two or three at the most
The same number as are in the Responsible role
content.stem: According to RACI philosophy, how many people can be in the Accountable role for a task?
content.why: The Accountable person is ultimately answerable for the successful completion of the task, so there can be only one person where “the buck stops here.” [I.B.2.d]

content.stem: Last month, a local company reported the following quality costs. Training $40,000 Material inspection $12,000 Test equipment $65,000 In-plant scrap and rework $15,000 What is the total appraisal cost for last month?
content.why: The items considered for appraisal costs include test equipment and material inspection, so the cost is $12,000 + $65,000 = $77,000. [II.E]

content.stem: Last month, a local company reported the following quality costs. Training $40,000 Material inspection $12,000 Test equipment $65,000 In-plant scrap and rework $15,000 What is the reported external failure cost for last month?
content.why: None of the costs listed are external failure costs; in-plant scrap and rework is an internal failure cost. [II.E]

content.stem: A quality system audit is to be conducted. This is an example of a(n):
content.why: Quality system audits fall under prevention costs. [II.E]

options: design and development of the curriculum, or training plan.
conducting a pretest for the participants.
assessing the need for the training.
content.stem: The first step in developing a training program is:
content.why: Before developing and implementing any training program, a needs analysis should be conducted to determine whether the training is actually needed and, if so, what it should consist of. [II.F]

options: Different knowledge levels of the participants
Training is problem-oriented rather than technique-oriented
content.stem: Which of the following is a reason for success of a training program?
content.why: Frank Gryna noted that it was best if participants could apply the training during the course to a problem of interest (be problem oriented). [II.F]

options: assessing the learner’s reaction to training.
determining the cost of the training.
content.stem: Pretests and posttests are useful tools in a training program for:
content.why: Pretests and posttests can be very useful for determining participant learning and retention of material. [II.F]

content.stem: Which of the following tools can be used for justifying and prioritizing projects?
content.why: Net present value is the only option used for justifying and prioritizing projects. [I.B.2.d]

content.stem: Suppose net present value (NPV) is to be estimated for a particular project. To determine how the NPV will change if the interest rate decreases or increases, for example, by 5%, one is doing a type of:
content.why: When metrics are examined by varying the inputs (such as percentage, rate, and so on) in NPV, this is a sensitivity analysis. [I.B.2.d]

content.stem: A Gantt chart is a useful:
content.why: A Gantt chart is also a milestone chart, a planning tool. [I.B.2.d]

content.stem: Which of the following systems is used to record critical data and control and monitor a process?
content.why: A quality information system is the collection of data, rules, and equipment that creates information about quality in a systematic way. [I.B.3]

content.stem: For any quality system, all quality-related activities begin with:
content.why: Throughout the product life cycle, understanding and identifying customer needs is the first and most important step in any quality-related activity. [II.A.1]

content.stem: The ASQ Code of Ethics primarily regulates its members’:
content.why: Per the ASQ Code of Ethics Introduction, the purpose of the Code is to establish global standards of conduct and behavior for its members, certification holders, and anyone else who may represent or be perceived to represent ASQ. [I.C]

content.stem: When citing the ASQ CQE certification on social media, one should make sure that their certification is:
content.why: The ASQ Code of Ethics requires members to accurately represent and not mislead others regarding professional qualifications, including education, titles, affiliations, and certifications; previous and future certifications do not hold the same credibility as current ones. [I.C]

content.stem: The ASQ Code of Ethics contains a statement that approves of:
content.why: The ASQ Code of Ethics contains a section directing members to act and conduct business in a professional and socially responsible manner; the other options would not be condoned. [I.C]

options: Filing a patent for your work
Hiring the best candidate for a job
Providing consulting on an unfamiliar topic
content.stem: Which of the following would be an ASQ Code of Ethics violation?
content.why: The ASQ Code of Ethics states members should offer services, provide advice, and undertake assignments only in their areas of competence, expertise, and training. [I.C]

content.stem: The most severe discipline resulting from an ASQ Code of Ethics violation is:
content.why: The ASQ Code of Ethics states disciplinary actions will be commensurate with the seriousness of the offense and may include permanent revocation of certifications and/or expulsion from the society. [I.C]

options: individuals begin to shift from personal concerns to the needs of the team.
the team’s mission is clarified and specific roles are identified.
team members still think and act as individuals instead of impacting as a team.
the team has matured and is working in the best interest of the team and team goals.
content.stem: Common development stages teams often progress through are known as forming, storming, norming, and performing. In the “storming” stage:
content.why: In the storming phase, teams become familiar with one another and have worked on missions and strategies, but members often still act in their own individual best interests rather than the team's as a whole. [I.D]

content.stem: Keeping the team on task is the main function of the team:
content.why: The facilitator's role is to provide support for the team, and the main task for that individual is to keep the team on task. [I.E.1]

options: discuss content issues with the team.
discuss process issues with the team.
suggest technical solutions to the team.
provide financial backing to the team.
content.stem: Part of the team facilitator’s mission is to:
content.why: The facilitator's role should be marginal and grow less important as the team matures. Overall, the facilitator is responsible for process issues, meeting agendas, communication among teams, and keeping the team on task. [I.E.1]

content.stem: A useful brainstorming tool for reducing a large list of items to a smaller, manageable one is:
content.why: The nominal group technique allows for brainstorming a large number of ideas or suggestions while providing everyone an equal voice in the process. [I.E.2]

content.stem: In the communication process, there are five methods of feedback: evaluation, interpretation, support, probing, and understanding. Of these methods, the one that most often creates defensiveness and can quickly break the communication process is:
content.why: All feedback methods can lead to a breakdown in the communication process; however, evaluation, which involves a judgment about the importance, worth, or appropriateness of the statement, is the one that leads to a breakdown much more quickly. [I.F]

content.stem: A quality manual generally consists of four tiers or layers that include:
content.why: The four tiers are policies, procedures, instructions, and records. The first or top tier represents policies. The second tier represents procedures. The third tier represents work instructions. The fourth tier represents a record of results of implementing a quality system. [II.B.1]

content.stem: Which of the following supplier management tools is used to initially verify that the supplier has adequate financial resources, manufacturing capabilities, and quality systems?
content.why: A supplier audit is not a bad option, but a supplier survey is better since it provides an initial assessment of a supplier's financial resources, manufacturing capabilities, and quality systems. [I.H]

options: Emphasis on a formal strategic plan for change
content.stem: Implementing quality improvement in an organization can be a failure for several reasons. Which of the following is one obstacle to implementing quality?
content.why: The ASQ Certified Quality Engineer Handbook, Fifth Edition, lists lack of real employee empowerment among the common barriers to a successful quality improvement implementation, along with lack of a formalized strategic plan, lack of strong motivation, and lack of customer focus, among others. [I.I]

content.stem: Consider a matrix with rows labeled Severity (Low, Medium, High) and columns labeled Probability (Low, Medium, High), used to plot the combination of likelihood and severity for identified risks. This table is an example of a(n):
content.why: The table represents a risk matrix (also known as a risk assessment matrix). It contains information on the probability of a certain level of risk and the level of severity. [VII.B.2]

options: Hazard analysis and critical control points (HACCP)
content.stem: Which of the following techniques uses guide words and is based on the assumption that risks are caused by deviations from the design plans?
content.why: HAZOP is the one technique that uses guide words and can be used to identify operability issues and potential hazards that may lead to unacceptable products, processes, or services. [VII.B.2]

content.stem: A new Quality Director is spearheading the establishment of a new Lean Production System at her company. She had previously encountered poor quality products and late deliveries from an overseas supplier and decided to set up a brainstorming session with her team for identifying and recording potential risk sources, causes, and potential consequences of using this overseas supplier to their lean and just in time (JIT) production. What process is being described here?
content.why: Risk identification is the process of finding, recognizing, describing, and recording risks, including the identification of risk sources, events, their causes, and their potential consequences. [VII.C.1]

options: maintain risk at or below an acceptable level.
content.stem: The purpose of risk control is to:
content.why: The main goal of risk control is to maintain the level of risk at an acceptably low level. [VII.C.1]

options: Obtaining new information to update risk levels and risk criteria
Determining the type of risk management applied
content.stem: Risk control requires documentation that addresses monitoring and review of risks and controls put in place. Which of the following would be part of monitoring and review?
content.why: Obtaining and applying new information should be included in any risk control documentation. [VII.C.1]

options: there are controls in place to address significant risks.
there is more than one control in place to address a significant risk.
there is no control in place to address a significant risk.
the control in place is sufficient.
content.stem: A gap may exist when controlling risks if:
content.why: A gap occurs when the control in place is not adequate for the risk, or no control has been put in place for a significant risk. [VII.C.1]

options: risk that remains after a risk treatment has been implemented.
risk due to a gap between what is believed to be risk and what really is risk.
unknown risk that can never be identified.
risk prior to the implementation of mitigations.
content.stem: Residual risk is:
content.why: Residual risk is that risk remaining even after a treatment of a known risk has been implemented; a risk treatment does not always eliminate a risk but may only minimize it until the risk is at or below an acceptable level. [VII.C.1]

content.stem: Risk reduction and risk acceptance are the two components of:
content.why: Risk reduction focuses on the avoidance of risk, while risk acceptance focuses on the decision to accept risk; together they are risk control. [VII.C.1]

options: monitoring techniques to correct sporadic problems.
an annual quality program to institutionalize managerial control and review.
a method that drives out fear so that everyone may work effectively.
a breakthrough sequence to solve chronic problems.
content.stem: According to the quality trilogy, quality improvement is:
content.why: In his 1964 text, Managerial Breakthrough, Juran defined quality improvement as a breakthrough sequence to solve chronic problems that is analogous to “common causes.” [I.A.1]

content.stem: The critical characteristics of any documentation of a quality system are:
content.why: Compliance, accuracy, and clarity; without these components, users will lose confidence in the documentation. [II.B.1]

content.stem: What activity is performed to verify that known risks are being controlled and that risk treatment plans in place are effective?
content.why: In addition to determining whether known risks are being controlled and risk treatment plans are effective, risk audits can also be helpful in identifying new risks. [VII.C.2]

content.stem: Avoiding risk, changing likelihood or consequences, and taking risk to pursue opportunity are actions that are addressed in:
content.why: See Clause 6.1.2 in ISO 9001:2015. [VII.C.3]

content.stem: Which of the following risk treatment options are available to designers and manufacturers of a hospital bed?
content.why: Share, accept, exploit, and enhance options are available only for positive risks. A hospital bed requires safety risk management and will have negative-risk treatment options available (avoid, mitigate, transfer, accept). [VII.C.3]

options: leading risk indicator for supplier quality.
leading risk indication for supplier timeliness.
leading risk indicator for transponder quality.
lagging risk indicator for transponder quality.
content.stem: A Key Risk Indicator (KRI) is a metric that provides a leading or lagging indication of the current state of risk exposure on key objectives. A manufacturing team assembles circuit boards for transponders. Certain capacitors for the circuit are being found to be faulty upon receipt by incoming quality inspectors, and Return Material Authorization (RMA) forms are often required. The number of RMA forms for a particular supplier is a:
content.why: The potential defective part is not yet installed in the transponder, so depending on the sampling of the supplier lot a bad part may be used; this makes the RMA forms a leading risk indicator for transponder quality. [VII.C.4]

content.stem: The risk management process step in which the effectiveness of the risk assessment techniques are evaluated is:
content.why: Evaluating the effectiveness of risk assessment techniques is one part of monitoring a risk management process, along with checking whether assumptions made when estimating risk are still valid and whether risk assessment results match actual results. [VII.C.4]

options: Agree with risk manager that off-label use is a safety risk and should be actively prevented by all means
Acknowledge that off-label use is a risk that is a positive risk and explore an avenue for exploitation using the clinical team’s researched data
Agree with marketing team and make plans to approve carotid indication in addition to femoral indication
Don’t take any action as current situation is making company money without legal or regulatory liability
content.stem: A medical catheter is approved in the U.S. by the FDA for femoral artery access only. However, physicians are using the device off label for carotid artery access. The clinical department has noticed several publications where carotid access has been performed and successful results published. The company’s risk manager states that off-label use is risk that needs to be mitigated. Your marketing team says that this is an opportunity to be capitalized upon. What is the most risk intelligent action to take?
content.why: It is wise to acknowledge the positive risk and make a well-informed, balanced decision; preventing it outright ignores the positive risk, and approving immediately or taking no action both skip proper risk identification, analysis, and evaluation. [VII.C.5]

content.stem: The main purpose of a risk mitigation plan is to:
content.why: Risk mitigation includes the act of attempting to minimize the risk's impact on the system, process, or product. [VII.C.5]

content.stem: If the response to a particular risk is to attempt to minimize its impact, this is known as:
content.why: A risk mitigation plan is implemented once risks have been identified and evaluated to determine whether the risk is worth eliminating or minimizing, or whether to accept the risk and do nothing about it. [VII.C.5]

options: Roll out Six Sigma methods on a project-by-project basis.
Begin at lower levels in the organization.
content.stem: Which of the following methods is the most effective way to implement Six Sigma in an organization?
content.why: A Six Sigma program that focuses on tools alone often lacks organization-wide buy-in and delivers limited results. A Six Sigma infrastructure gives employees both the tools and the problem-solving methods needed for specific projects identified by management. [V.C]

content.stem: Which of the following tools is typically used to identify waste in a lean system?
content.why: The goal of a lean system is to eliminate waste from a process. A value stream map, a visual representation of all the steps in a process including timing, is one of the first tools used to identify improvement opportunities and value-added vs. non-value-added activities. [V.D]

options: implementation of a documented quality system.
content.stem: One major component of a quality system is:
content.why: Effective implementation of a quality system that has been reviewed and approved for release is one of the two major components of a quality program. The other component is documentation of procedures and instructions of the quality system. [II.A.1]

content.stem: A restaurant is analyzing its current workflow. Employees in the restaurant must walk back and forth throughout the kitchen to retrieve various cooking tools during preparation of a meal. How might the restaurant classify this action?
content.why: Employees walking more than necessary to retrieve supplies is an example of waste due to excess motion; a redesigned kitchen layout moving tools closer to where they're needed would reduce the excess walking. [V.D]

content.stem: The restaurant is also examining its front-of-house operations. They found that there is frequently a long line of customers standing by the chicken counter while staff turn over tables. What kind of waste is occurring at the front of house at this restaurant?
content.why: Customers waiting to be seated due to long table setup/turnover times is waste due to waiting; cross-training staff or standardized work could reduce setup time and customer wait. [V.D]

content.stem: After creating a value stream map of a process, on which steps in the process should a quality team focus their efforts?
content.why: Non-value-added activities are steps in a process that aren't needed; improvement projects have the largest impact when focused on these steps. [V.D]

options: To make slow, incremental changes to a process
To reduce defects produced in a process
content.stem: What is the primary goal of 5S?
content.why: 5S stands for five Japanese words for organizing a workplace: sort, set in order, shine, standardize, and sustain. Reengineering radically changes a process and kaizen makes slow, incremental changes; neither is 5S's goal. [V.D]

content.stem: A toy company paints a certain toy white by default. The toys are then painted other colors as requested by customers. As what type of waste might a quality team classify this action?
content.why: Painting toys white by default and then repainting per customer request is waste due to excess processing; painting only after the customer's color choice is known would eliminate the extra processing step. [V.D]

options: The weakest step in a chain of processes is improved.
There is less inventory and a smoother flow of supplies.
Products are not processed until a customer places an order.
content.stem: What is the main benefit of implementing a kanban system?
content.why: A kanban system provides visual cues that ease restocking, resulting in less inventory and a smoother flow of supplies. Theory of Constraints improves the weakest step in a process chain, 5S organizes a workplace, and a pull system completes steps only when triggered by demand. [V.D]

content.stem: A deli has newly instituted a few changes to its work area. The workers now have a schedule for cleaning their workstations, have standardized practices, and have created designated locations for all their equipment. What improvement method has this deli employed?
content.why: 5S is five words adapted from Japanese for organizing a workplace: arranging things properly, orderliness, cleanliness, cleanup, and discipline. A cleaning schedule, standardized practices, and designated equipment locations are the deli implementing the five S's. [V.D]

content.stem: A factory uses an illuminated indicator light when a certain process is in progress. This is an example of:
content.why: A visible signal like a light is an example of visual control, cueing employees that an action is being performed and helping create a safer or more efficient workplace. [V.D]

content.stem: In a convenience store, items are stacked in front of a card that lists details on the product, including the location of additional boxes in their storage room as well as a number to call to reorder. What type of system has this convenience store implemented?
content.why: A kanban system uses visual cues to trigger resupply; when a bin empties, the card alerts the employee where to find or how to order more supplies. [V.D]

content.stem: To complete a process, parts must travel through four departments located in different areas of a manufacturing facility. As what type of waste would a quality team at the facility classify this process?
content.why: Parts traveling through departments spread across a facility is waste due to excess movement of material; grouping assembly processes together would reduce the distance components travel. [V.D]

content.stem: Once a quality manual is complete, a final review is in order. The reviewed copy should be endorsed and authorized for release by:
content.why: Top management is responsible for endorsing the content of the final document as well as authorizing its release for use. [II.B.2]

content.stem: A manufacturing facility has painted arrows on the floor to show the flow of products through the facility. Which lean tool has this facility implemented?
content.why: Painted arrows showing product flow are an example of visual control, giving employees quick visual cues that help movement and reduce errors or accidents. [V.D]

content.stem: The principle that each process should be done the same way, every time, by every employee is called:
content.why: Standardized work means every step or activity is done the same way every time, reducing process variation and producing a more consistent product or service. [V.D]

content.stem: Which of the following lean tools measures the time from the last good part of one type to the first good part of the next?
content.why: Single-minute exchange of die (SMED) reduces machine changeover times, cutting the time required to switch a machine or assembly line to a different product. [V.D]

content.stem: What is the difference between cycle time and takt time?
content.why: Cycle time is the time it takes to complete an activity or process step. Takt time is based on customer demand: Takt time = (Time available) / (Units required), the average time a process should take per unit to meet demand. [V.D]

content.stem: A shoe company routinely makes more components than are needed when assembling its product. As what type of waste might this company classify this action?
content.why: Routinely making more components than needed is waste due to overproduction; the company should adjust production of this component to match actual need. [V.D]

content.stem: A university has released a document detailing all the required actions instructors should take when proctoring an exam. All instructors across the university are expected to follow these directions. What tool has the university implemented?
content.why: A document requiring all instructors to follow the same exam procedure every time is standardized work, intended to make the process run more smoothly and consistently across the university. [V.D]

content.stem: A company has received an order for 550 items that it needs to produce in an eight-hour workday. In seconds, what is the takt time for this product?
content.why: Takt time = (Time available) / (Units required). Time available is 8 x 60 x 60 = 28,800 seconds, so takt time = 28,800 / 550 = 52.36 seconds. [V.D]

content.stem: A caterer had a lunch order for a group of 50 people and had two hours to complete the order. However, after two hours, the caterer was only able to complete 45 lunches. Which of the following must be true?
content.why: The caterer's takt time is 2 x 60 / 50 = 2.4 minutes per lunch. Since only 45 of 50 lunches were completed in two hours, the actual cycle time must have been greater than the takt time. [V.D]

content.stem: A radiation clinic treats patients with different types of cancer. The position of each patient on the table is different depending on the type of cancer. Therefore, after one patient is treated, another patient, requiring a different setup than the previous patient, arrives. Which lean tool would best help a quality team in this clinic?
content.why: SMED reduces changeover times; although introduced in a factory setting, the same methodology applies to the clinic's required changeover time between patients needing different table setups. [V.D]

content.stem: A supplier has received an order from one of its customers. It must complete an order of 750 items in a daytime shift that is 10 hours long. The cycle time for this process is 50 seconds. Without any changes in its current production, will the supplier be able to meet the customer’s demands?
content.why: The supplier's takt time is 10 x 60 x 60 / 750 = 48 seconds. Because the cycle time (50 seconds) is greater than the takt time, the supplier is unlikely to meet customer demand without production adjustments. [V.D]

content.why: The six big losses in OEE include two speed losses: idling and minor stoppage, and reduced speed. [V.D]

content.stem: If an eight-hour shift corresponds to 480 minutes, what is the availability of a machine with the following information: • There are two breaks of 15 minutes each. • The machine broke down for 35 minutes. • The adjustment time was 10 minutes.
content.why: Loading time = 480 - 15 - 15 = 450 minutes. Unplanned downtime = 35 + 10 = 45 minutes. Availability = (Loading Time - Unplanned Downtime) / Loading Time x 100 = (450-45)/450 x 100 = 90%. [V.D]

content.stem: What is one of the most common causes of failures in problem solving?
content.why: One of the most frequent sources of failure in problem-solving is a poor definition of the problem; problem statements should be clear, focused, fact-based, and establish what is known, unknown, and needs to be done. [V.E]

content.stem: During the correction phase of the corrective action cycle, which of the following is instrumental in success?
content.why: In the correction phase of the corrective action cycle, an optimal solution is developed to solve the problem, and creativity is essential to doing this well. [V.E]

content.stem: A team in a food production plant has recently instituted changes to one of their bottling processes. What should the team do to avoid the process backsliding?
content.why: The recurrence control phase involves standardizing the solution and identifying the key variables that need to be kept under control to avoid backsliding. [V.E]

content.stem: In which phase of the corrective action cycle does a team seek to continuously improve the performance of a process by holding regular reviews of the process?
content.why: In the effectiveness assessment phase of the corrective action cycle, the team continues monitoring the process through regular reviews to identify additional opportunities for improvement. [V.E]

content.why: Poka-yoke, from Japan, is also known as error-proofing, a preventive technique used to prevent errors from occurring. [V.F]

content.stem: A food company produces cookie dough. All a customer must do is slice the cookie dough and bake it in their oven for approximately eight minutes. The company’s cookie dough recipe was developed so that the cookie quality is not vastly affected by differences in ovens, elevation, or other environmental conditions. content.why: A recipe whose quality isn't greatly affected by differing use conditions (oven, elevation) is an example of robust design, which reduces variation in quality under various use conditions. [V.F]

content.stem: A printer that will only run when the paper trays are closed is an example of which of the following concepts?
content.why: A printer that won't run with an open paper tray is poka-yoke, or error-proofing, preventing paper jams or other errors before they occur. [V.F]

content.stem: Before the next step in a process, a sorting machine is used to remove components that are above the upper specification limit. What principle of error- proofing is implemented in this process?
content.why: Detection is the error-proofing principle where a defect is caught before it moves to the next process step; the sorting machine removing out-of-spec components before the next step is detection. [V.F]

content.why: "A" represents the primary datum. [III.C]

content.stem: 450 electrical components for a machine were subjected to a reliability test. The observed failures during 100-hour intervals: 0-100 hrs, 7 failures; 100-200 hrs, 16 failures; 200-300 hrs, 19 failures; 300-400 hrs, 27 failures. What is the estimated reliability at time t = 200?
content.why: The estimated reliability at time t = 200 is R̂(t) = n2/N = 427/450 = 0.9489, where n2 = 450 - 16 - 7 = 427 is the number of units that have not yet failed by 200 hours. [III.E.1]

content.stem: Using the same 450-component reliability test (100-hour interval failure counts: 0-100 hrs 7, 100-200 hrs 16, 200-300 hrs 19, 300-400 hrs 27), what is the estimated failure density for time 300 < t < 400?
content.why: The failure density is f̂(t) = (n3 - n4)/((t4 - t3) x N) = (408-381)/((400-300) x 450) = 0.0006, using the number of survivors at 300 hours (408) and 400 hours (381). [III.E.1]

content.stem: Using the same 450-component reliability test (100-hour interval failure counts: 0-100 hrs 7, 100-200 hrs 16, 200-300 hrs 19, 300-400 hrs 27), what is the instantaneous rate of failure for time 300 < t < 400?
content.why: The instantaneous rate of failure is ĥ(t) = f̂(t)/R̂(t) = (n3-n4)/((t4-t3) x n3) = (408-381)/((400-300) x 408) = 0.00066. [III.E.1]

content.stem: A series system is composed of five subsystems, each with reliability 0.995. What is the reliability of the system?
content.why: A series system's reliability is the product of its components' reliabilities: Rs(t) = 0.995^5 = 0.9752. [III.E.2]

content.stem: Which of the following is the subject of one of the standards in the ISO 9000 Systems family?
content.why: Quality management is one of the standards, while the others are subjects of other standards (environmental management, risk management) or a quality management principle (continuous improvement). [II.C]

content.stem: A parallel system is composed of five subsystems, each with reliability 0.995. The reliability of this system is closest to which of the following values?
content.why: A parallel system fails only when all units fail: Rs(t) = 1 - [(1-0.995)]^5 = 0.999999, essentially 1. [III.E.2]

content.stem: In a series system consisting of three subsystems, each with a reliability of 0.75, if one subsystem fails, what is the probability that the entire system will fail?
content.why: A series system is made up of n components connected in series, so the system fails if any one of the components or subsystems fails. [III.E.2]

content.stem: What is the reliability of a series system with two subsystems, each with a reliability of 0.80?
content.why: Series-system reliability is the product of the subsystem reliabilities: Rs(t) = 0.80 x 0.80 = 0.64. [III.E.2]

content.stem: A machine has six subsystems and will fail when four or more of these subsystems fail. Each subsystem has a reliability of 0.88. What is the reliability of the machine?
content.why: This is a k-out-of-n system with k=3, n=6, p=0.88. Summing the binomial terms for 3, 4, 5, and 6 subsystems surviving gives Rs(t) = 0.02355 + 0.1295 + 0.3799 + 0.4644 = 0.9975. [III.E.2]

content.stem: A machine has a standby system design with three identical components in standby mode. Each component has a constant rate of failure λ = 0.08. What is the reliability of the machine at 100 hours of continuous operation?
content.why: For a standby system with n=4 standby components (original plus 3 standby), λ=0.08, t=100: Rs(t) = e^-8 x Σ(8^i/i!) for i=0 to 3 ≈ 0.0424. [III.E.2]

content.stem: 750 machines were tested for five hours. 28 failures occurred. What is the failure rate for these machines?
content.why: The failure rate λ = failures / total test time = 28/(750 x 5) = 0.0075. [III.E.2]

content.stem: The reliability of a component at t = 400 hours is 0.645. Assuming that the reliability of this component is exponential, which of the following is closest to the mean time to failure (MTTF)?
content.why: Given R(400)=0.645 and R(t)=e^-λt, solving -400λ=ln(0.645) gives λ≈0.0011, so MTTF = 1/λ ≈ 909, or about 910 hours. [III.E.2]

content.stem: The MTTF for a model of dishwasher is 115 months. What is the reliability that a randomly selected dishwasher of this model type survives past 115 months? Assume that the reliability function is an exponential distribution.
content.why: MTTF = 1/failure rate = 115 months, so λ = 1/115. Since reliability is exponential, R(115) = e^-115/115 = e^-1 = 0.3679. [III.E.2]

content.stem: The MTTF for a machine is 525 hours. What fraction of machines survives past 1,000 hours? Assume that the reliability of the machine has an exponential distribution.
content.why: With MTTF = 525 and λ = 1/525, R(1000) = e^-1000/525 ≈ 0.1488, so approximately 15% of machines survive past 1,000 hours. [III.E.2]

content.stem: What is the probability a randomly selected rechargeable battery fails by six hours if the mean time between failures (MTBF) is five hours? Assume that the reliability of the component is exponentially distributed.
content.why: With MTBF = 5 hours, λ = 1/5 = 0.2. The probability the battery fails by time t is F(t) = 1 - R(t) = 1 - e^-λt, so F(6) = 1 - e^(-6/5) ≈ 0.6988. [III.E.2]

content.stem: The ISO 9000 series of standards emphasizes eight quality management principles. Which of the following would be categorized as one of those principles?
content.why: Customer focus is one of the quality management principles emphasized by the ISO 9000 family. The other choices do not represent an ISO quality management principle. [II.C]

content.stem: If the MTBF of a component is 900 hours, what is the reliability of this component at 500 hours? Assume that the reliability of the component is exponentially distributed.
The failure rate of a machine is 0.0008. Assuming the life distribution of this type of machine is exponential, what fraction of machines in the population survives longer than the MTTF?
content.why: With λ=0.0008, MTTF = 1/λ = 1,250. R(MTTF) = e^-0.0008(1250) = 0.3679, so 36.79% of components survive past the mean time to failure. [III.E.2]

content.stem: The failure rate of a machine is 0.0008. Assuming the life distribution of this type of machine is exponential and the MTTR is five hours, what is the steady-state availability of this machine?
content.why: With λ=0.0008, MTBF = 1/λ = 1,250 hours. With MTTR = 5 hours, steady-state availability A = MTBF/(MTBF+MTTR) = 1250/1255 ≈ 0.996. [III.E.2]

content.stem: In a test of a repairable component of a machine, 600 components were tested for 25 hours, and 515 components failed. If the mean time to repair (MTTR) these components is eight hours, what is the steady-state availability of this component?
content.why: λ = failures/total test time = 515/(600x25) = 0.0343, so MTBF = 1/λ ≈ 29.13 hours. With MTTR = 8 hours, availability A = MTBF/(MTBF+MTTR) = 29.13/37.13 ≈ 0.7845. [III.E.2]

content.stem: Which type of maintenance policy creates a situation where there will be the maximum run time between repairs?
content.why: A corrective maintenance policy does not require repairs or preventive maintenance until a failure occurs, which allows for the maximum run time between repairs. [III.E.2]

content.stem: In the second region identified in the general failure rate model (the bathtub curve), what is the most common cause for failures?
content.why: The second region of a bathtub curve is the constant-failure-rate region, characterized by the inherent failure rate of a product's components (random failures). [III.E.3]

content.stem: Which of the following probability distributions is often used to model the second region of the bathtub curve?
content.why: The exponential distribution is the only distribution with a constant failure rate, so it is often used to model the second (constant-failure-rate) region of the bathtub curve. [III.E.3]

content.stem: Which of the following probability distributions is often used to model the third region of the bathtub curve?
content.why: The third region of the bathtub curve, the wear-out region, has an increasing failure rate over time, which is often modeled using the Weibull distribution. [III.E.3]

content.why: The main goal of an FMEA is to help a team identify and eliminate the negative effects of a potential failure before it occurs. [III.E.4]

content.stem: A hospital is preparing to do an FMEA for a surgical procedure. Which of the following groups of employees should make up the FMEA team members?
content.why: An FMEA team should be a cross section of employees across several fields; at minimum, a surgical-procedure FMEA team should include a doctor, nurse, technician, engineer, business office employee, and manager. [III.E.4]

content.stem: Which of the following ISO standards are guidelines only?
content.why: ISO 9004 consists of suggestions only, guidelines but not requirements for certification. [II.C]

content.stem: Which risk management tool contains the following elements: potential failure types, the risk associated with the failures, and risk mitigations?
content.why: An FMEA contains all of these elements: potential failure types, associated risk, and risk mitigations. [III.E.4]

content.stem: An FMEA team has identified a potential failure and assessed the following score for severity, occurrence, and detection for this failure mode: 8, 2, 7. What is the RPN for this failure mode?
content.why: RPN is the product of severity, occurrence, and detection: RPN = 8 x 2 x 7 = 112. [III.E.4]

content.stem: An FMEA team calculated an RPN of 112 (severity 8, occurrence 2, detection 7) for a failure mode. If the risk reduction threshold is an RPN of 40, which of the following risk ratings for a different failure mode would indicate a situation requiring risk reduction?
content.why: Given a risk reduction threshold of 40 (and the RPN=112 example above), the first three options each yield an RPN below 40. Option d gives RPN = 3 x 4 x 4 = 48, which exceeds the threshold and requires risk reduction. [III.E.4]

content.stem: Which of the following risk analyses considers product failures by a customer due to human factors?
content.why: A use FMEA (uFMEA) specifically considers customers' human-factors-related product failures. [III.E.4]

content.stem: Which of the following types of FMEA is created after the others?
content.why: The process FMEA (pFMEA) is initiated last, closer to the end of design and development, after the use, design, and system FMEAs have already been created, since the product must be designed before the process to make it. [III.E.4]

content.stem: Which of the following types of failure mode and effects analyses would best be used to assess the risk of insufficient product instructions in detail?
content.why: Product instructions are part of the user interface and are best analyzed in detail through a use FMEA (uFMEA). [III.E.4]

content.stem: In addition to the two main components of risk, the FMEA technique may add a rating scale for:
content.why: The two main components of risk in FMEA are probability of occurrence (likelihood) and impact (severity); detection is the third rating scale often added. [III.E.4]

content.stem: An event that would be analyzed for impact and likelihood in a use failure mode and effects analysis (uFMEA) is:
content.why: Adequacy of visual alarms is part of the user interface, evaluated via a use FMEA (uFMEA); the other options are better suited to a design FMEA or process FMEA. [III.E.4]

content.why: An FMECA is an assessment of risk that develops a prioritization scheme for corrective action based on the severity and occurrence of failure modes. [III.E.4]

content.stem: A company compares two competing sampling plans using their OC (operating characteristic) curves. Curve A drops off more steeply as the lot percentage defective increases, meaning its probability of accepting the lot falls much faster than Curve B's. Compared to Curve B, Curve A:
content.why: The dashed OC curve is better for the company. As the percentage nonconforming increases, its probability of accepting the lot decreases much faster than the other curve, so the company will accept fewer unacceptable lots from the producer. [IV.C.1]

content.stem: The Malcolm Baldrige National Quality Award consists of how many key criteria for performance excellence?
content.why: There are seven criteria: Leadership; Strategy; Customers; Measurement, Analysis, and Knowledge Management; Workforce; Operations; and Results. [II.C]

content.stem: A double sampling plan is implemented with the following parameters: n = 50, c = 1, r = 4, n = 75, c = 3, r = 6 1 1 1 2 2 2 What is the probability that a decision is made (to accept or reject the lot) on the first sample if the percentage nonconforming, p, is equal to 0.10?
content.why: The lot is accepted or rejected on the first sample unless 2 or 3 defects are found (which triggers a second sample). P(decision on first sample) = 1 - P(d=2) - P(d=3) = 1 - 0.0779 - 0.1386 = 0.7835. [IV.C.2]

content.stem: A double sampling plan is implemented with the following parameters: n = 50, c = 1, r = 3, n = 75, c = 3, r = 4 1 1 1 2 2 2 What is the average sample number for this sampling plan if the percentage nonconforming, p, is equal to 0.10?
content.why: The probability of requiring a second sample is 1 - 0.7835 = 0.2165 (from the previous question). Average sample number = n1 + n2 x P2 = 50 + 75 x 0.2165 = 66.24, or 67. [IV.C.2]

content.stem: When compared with sampling plans with equal protection, the average sample number of double sampling plans generally is:
content.why: When quality is very good or very poor, the average sample size of double sampling plans is generally smaller than plans with equal protection, since decisions are more often made on the first sample, requiring fewer second samples. [IV.C.2]

content.stem: Which of the following types of sampling are allowed in ANSI/ASQ Z1.4-2003 (R2018)?
content.why: ANSI/ASQ Z1.4-2003 (R2018) allows single sampling, double sampling, and multiple sampling. [IV.C.2]

content.stem: A lot size of 1,500 is to be inspected using ANSI/ASQ Z1.4-2003 (R2018). The AQL is 0.40%. What is the required sample size for a single sampling plan (normal, level II inspection)?
content.why: For a lot size of 1,500, the sample size code letter for normal, level II inspection is K; following ANSI/ASQ Z1.4-2003 (R2018) Table II-A, the required sample size is n = 315. [IV.C.2]

content.stem: A lot size of 500 is to be inspected using ANSI/ASQ Z1.4-2003 (R2018). The AQL is 0.65%. What are the required sample size, acceptance number, and rejection number for a single sampling plan (normal level II inspection)?
content.why: For a lot size of 500, the code letter for normal, level II inspection is H; at AQL 0.65%, Table II-A's downward arrow points to code letter J, giving a sample size of 80, acceptance number 1, and rejection number 2. [IV.C.2]

content.stem: A lot of size 200 is to be inspected using ANSI/ASQ Z1.4-2003 (R2018). The AQL is 0.65%. What are the required sample sizes for a double sampling plan (normal, level II inspection)?
content.why: For a lot size of 200, the code letter for normal, level II inspection is G; Table III-A (Double Sampling Plans for Normal Inspection) gives a sample size of 20 for both the first and second sample, regardless of AQL. [IV.C.2]

content.stem: A lot of size 400 is to be inspected using ANSI/ASQ Z1.4-2003 (R2018). The AQL is 0.65%. For the first sample of a double sampling plan (normal, level II inspection), what are the acceptance and rejection numbers?
content.why: For a lot size of 400, the code letter for normal, level II inspection is H; at AQL 0.65%, Table III-A's downward arrow points to code letter J, giving a first-sample acceptance number of 0 and rejection number of 2. [IV.C.2]

content.why: Variables sampling plans offer equal protection with a much smaller sample size than attribute sampling plans, though they are generally more expensive to implement, harder to administer, and can only monitor one quality characteristic at a time. [IV.C.2]

content.stem: A lot of 100 items is submitted for inspection under ANSI/ASQ Z1.9-2003 (R2018), level II, normal inspection with AQL = 0.65%. Both upper and lower specification limits are specified for these items. What sample size is required for this sampling plan?
content.why: ANSI/ASQ Z1.9-2003 (R2018) Table A-2 gives sample size code letter F for this lot; Table B-3 shows code letter F corresponds to a sample size of 10, regardless of AQL level. [IV.C.2]

content.why: Sample integrity ensures a product has not been misused or contaminated and that the sample accurately represents the entire lot. [IV.C.3]

content.stem: Which of the following types of control are methods used to maintain sample integrity?
content.why: Sample integrity is maintained through batch control (documenting production steps and unique batch IDs), change control (tracking product changes), and configuration control (an extension of change control). [IV.C.3]

content.why: Dimensional inspection determines whether a product's measurements conform or don't conform to specifications; it does not by itself determine the product's overall quality, which depends on design and manufacturing. [IV.D.1]

content.why: A sine bar provides more precise angular measurement than protractors, bevel protractors, or squares. [IV.D.1]
