content.stem: A part was inspected using a go/no-go gage. The part did not mate with either end of the gage. Did the part pass the inspection?
content.why: A part passes a go/no-go inspection only if it mates with the go end and not the no-go end. Since this part did not mate with either end, it failed the go inspection and should be rejected. [IV.D.1]

content.stem: Which of the following methods is the most common for surface measurements?
content.why: Stylus averaging, used to measure an average electrical signal, is the most common surface measurement method because it is fast, repeatable, interpretable, and relatively inexpensive. [IV.D.1]

content.stem: A key component of a part is round in shape. Which of the following measurement tools is most appropriate to measure this component?
content.why: Precision spindle instruments are used for roundness measurements; calipers are for linear measurements, ring gages assess outside-dimension conformance, and dial indicators are used to check alignment or runout. [IV.D.1]

content.stem: The maximum tensile strength a particular part can withstand is an important quality characteristic of this part. Which of the following is most appropriate to test this quality characteristic?
content.why: Measuring maximum tensile strength destroys the part, so screening or 100% inspection isn't appropriate; nondestructive testing is required for this quality characteristic. [IV.D.2]

options: Eliminate work standards that prescribe numerical quotas.
Institute barriers that stand between the hourly worker and his right to pride of workmanship.
50% of quality problems are due to employees.
15% of quality problems are due to management.
content.stem: Which of the following is one of Deming’s 14 points?
content.why: Deming argued that work standards that include numerical quotas do nothing to motivate the common worker and should be eliminated. [I.A.1]

content.stem: The most comprehensive type of audit is the:
content.why: A quality system audit is an audit of the entire system. The other three are more specific and smaller in scope. [II.D.1]

content.stem: Which of the following nondestructive tests can only be used on parts made of iron and steel?
content.why: Magnetic particle testing works only on parts that can be magnetized, such as those made of iron, steel, or allied materials. [IV.D.2]

content.stem: Which of the following nondestructive tests can only be used on parts made of conductive materials?
content.why: Eddy current testing applies an AC current through a coil near the part's surface, so it can only be used on conductive materials. [IV.D.2]

content.stem: Which of the following organizations maintains the standards of measurement in the United States?
content.why: The National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) maintains the standards of measurement in the United States. [IV.E]

content.stem: Physical artifacts, paper standards, and definition of base units are elements of what field?
content.why: Physical artifacts (like gage blocks), paper standards (published specifications and methods), and definitions of base units are all foundational elements of metrology. [IV.E]

options: As a physical artifact used for direct reference
The amount of water required to fill a 36-ounce beaker
Based on the weight of carbon molecules
content.stem: How does NIST define the kilogram, the base unit of mass?
content.why: The kilogram is the only base SI unit still defined by a physical artifact, a platinum-iridium cylinder held by the International Bureau of Weights and Measures in Paris, with a duplicate protected by NIST in the U.S. [IV.E]

content.stem: Slight changes in temperature where parts are measured for conformance could lead to:
content.why: Ambient fluctuations like slight temperature changes are classified as random error, unpredictable accidental fluctuations, as opposed to systematic error (e.g., operator or calibration error). [IV.E]

content.stem: To tie a laboratory’s measurement standard to national standards, a company could use which of the following?
content.why: Traceability ties a laboratory's measurement standards to national standards. [IV.E]

content.stem: Information on the contribution to error of technicians or a laboratory’s procedures can typically be found in:
content.why: Measurement assurance protocols detail a measuring instrument's accuracy and the contribution to error from technicians, the lab environment, and lab procedures. [IV.E]

content.stem: The goal of equipment calibration is to maintain the system’s:
content.why: The goal of equipment calibration is to maintain a measurement system's accuracy. [IV.E]

content.stem: While analyzing repeated measurements of a quality characteristic, an employee notices that the values are consistently larger than the reference value. Which of the following has occurred in this measurement process?
content.why: Systematic error remains relatively constant across repeated measurements and can be caused by humans, imprecise devices, or poor manufacturing methods; values consistently larger than the reference value indicate systematic error, not random error (inherent fluctuations) or Type I/II error (which apply to hypothesis testing). [IV.F]

options: To meet requirements for certification to a management standard
Verification of conformance with contractual requirements
To contribute to the improvement of the management system
To maintain confidence in the capability of a supplier
content.stem: Which of the following would be a purpose for an internal quality audit?
content.why: Internal audits can be used to determine improvement opportunities for the quality management system. The other options apply to various types of external audits. [II.D.1]

content.stem: Which of the following components of a measurement system contributes to its accuracy?
content.why: A measurement system's accuracy consists of gage bias, linearity, and stability; repeatability and reproducibility describe its precision instead. [IV.F]

content.stem: Which of the following increases measurement system error?
content.why: Measurement system error can be attributed to gage bias, stability, linearity, repeatability, and reproducibility; correlation instead measures the linear relationship between two quantitative variables and doesn't contribute to measurement error. [IV.F]

content.stem: The length of a part should be 6.00 cm. A particular part is repeatedly measured six times, yielding the following measurements: 6.05, 5.94, 5.98, 6.01, 6.03, 5.97. What is the resulting bias for this part?
content.why: Bias = observed average - reference value. The observed average = (6.05+5.94+5.98+6.01+6.03+5.97)/6 = 5.997, so bias = 5.997 - 6.00 = -0.003. [IV.F]

options: There is evidence of nonlinearity in this measurement system.
There is evidence of stability issues in this measurement system.
The measurement system is not reproducible.
The measurement system is not repeatable.
content.stem: The lengths of three parts have the following reference values: 3.00 cm, 6.00 cm, 12.00 cm. Ten repeated measurements were taken for each type of part. The observed averages of these three samples were: 2.998, 5.843, 12.275. Which of the following statements is true?
content.why: Computing bias (observed average - reference value) for each part size shows -0.002, -0.157, and 0.275 as reference value increases from 3 to 12 cm; bias worsening as part size increases indicates nonlinearity in the measurement system. [IV.F]

options: the difference between the recorded measurement and the target value of a quality characteristic.
the variability present when the same part is measured multiple times under the same conditions.
the ability to get the same degree of bias in a measurement over time.
the ability to get the same degree of bias in a measurement for parts of different sizes.
content.stem: The precision of a measurement system can be defined as:
content.why: Precision is the variability observed when the same part is repeatedly measured under identical conditions using the same system; it is made up of repeatability and reproducibility, distinct from accuracy (closeness to the target/reference value). [IV.F]

content.stem: In a gage R&R study, the variance associated with repeatability was found to be 0.8842 and the variance associated with reproducibility was found to be 0.2466. What is the variance associated with measurement error?
content.why: Measurement error variance = reproducibility variance + repeatability variance = 0.8842 + 0.2466 = 1.1308. [IV.F]

content.stem: The ANOVA table below displays the results of a gage R&R study where two operators measured five parts three times each using the same gage. Source df SS MS F p Part 4 44 11 12.69 0.015 Operator 1 0.033 0.033 0.04 0.854 Part × Operator 4 3.467 0.867 0.70 0.599 Error 20 24.667 1.233 Total 29 72.167 Using this full model, what is the measurement error variability?
content.why: Using the ANOVA table's mean squares, the operator and part x operator variance components come out negative and are set to 0, leaving repeatability (error) variance = MSE = 1.233 as the full measurement error variability. [IV.F]

options: There is a significant interaction between parts and operators.
More operator training is necessary in this process.
The variation associated with repeatability should be investigated.
content.stem: A gage R&R study measured two operators on five parts, three replicates each. The full ANOVA model found: repeatability (error) variance = 1.233 (40.28% of total gage R&R variation), reproducibility variance = 0 (0%), and part-to-part variance = 1.828 (59.72%). The p-values show no significant operator effect and no significant part x operator interaction. Based on these results, which of the following statements is true?
content.why: The ANOVA table shows no significant operator effect or part x operator interaction, but repeatability accounts for a large share (40.28%) of total gage R&R variation, indicating the variation associated with repeatability should be investigated. [IV.F]

content.stem: From the same gage R&R study (measurement error variance = 1.233), suppose the upper and lower specification limits for the quality characteristic are 30 and 10, respectively. What is the precision-to-tolerance ratio for this process?
content.why: From the prior gage R&R study, measurement error variance = 1.233. Precision-to-tolerance ratio PTR = 6√1.233 / (30-10) = 0.333. [IV.F]

options: There are significant differences between operators.
The operators are consistent in their use of the gage.
The gage is not able to distinguish between parts.
The gage is able to distinguish between parts.
content.stem: A gage R&R study was performed for a process using ten parts, two operators, and three replicates. The resulting R-chart by operator shows: UCL = 9.27, R̄ = 3.6, LCL = 0, with every sample range for both operators falling within these control limits. What conclusions can be drawn from this control chart?
content.why: An R-chart by operator with UCL = 9.27, R̄ = 3.6, and LCL = 0 shows no points outside the control limits for either operator, indicating the operators are consistent in their use of the gage with no special causes of variation. [IV.F]

options: management where the corrective measures are needed.
line workers where the corrective measures are needed.
content.stem: A quality audit has been conducted and some corrective measures are recommended. The party responsible for planning and implementing these measures is:
content.why: The organization or company being audited (auditee) is responsible for making sure the corrective measures identified are addressed. [II.D.2]

content.stem: Which of the following distributions best describes the data set below? Goodness of Fit Test Results Normal Weibull AD = 1.456 AD = 0.214 p < 0.005 p > 0.250 Exponential Gamma AD = 1.456 AD = 0.581 p < 0.003 p = 0.152
content.why: The goodness-of-fit test determines which distribution best fits a data set, based on probability plot fit and/or the test's p-value. Of the four distributions tested, Weibull has the highest p-value (p > 0.250), making it the best fit. [VI.A.3]

content.stem: Which of the following descriptive statistics are typically found in a box plot?
content.why: A box plot divides a sorted data set using the minimum, Q1, median, Q3, and maximum; the mean is not typically identified on a box plot. [VI.A.7]

options: The normal distribution is not a reasonable model for the time to failure.
The Weibull distribution is a reasonable model for the time to failure.
The normal distribution is a reasonable model for the time to failure.
Not enough information is provided to draw conclusions.
content.stem: A team measured the time to failure of twenty components and plotted the data on a normal probability plot. The plotted points do not fall along a straight line. What conclusions can be drawn from this plot?
content.why: A normal distribution is a reasonable model only if the data points on a normal probability plot fall along a straight line. Since the plotted points do not fall in a straight line, the normal distribution is not an appropriate model for the time to failure. [VI.A.7]

content.stem: The contingency table below describes the relationship between the number of nonconforming components produced and time of day. Conforming Nonconforming Time parts parts Totals Day 94 5 99 Evening 87 10 97 Overnight 65 23 88 Totals 246 38 284 Given that a part is made overnight, what is the probability it is nonconforming?
content.why: P(nonconforming | overnight) = P(nonconforming and overnight) / P(overnight) = (23/284) / (88/284) = 23/88 ≈ 0.26. [VI.B.3]

content.stem: Suppose the number of errors in an invoice at a company has the probability mass function (written in table form) shown below. What is the expected number of errors in a randomly selected invoice? Number of errors X 0 1 2 3 4 Probability 0.86 0.06 0.04 0.03 0.01

A bottling factory claims that the volume of soda filled in bottles is 18 oz. You want to test whether the true mean volume of soda is different than 18 oz. The volume of a random sample of twenty-four bottles had a mean of 17.98 oz. with a standard deviation of 0.03 oz. Using a significance level of 5%, what is the appropriate test statistic for this hypothesis test?

options: There is not sufficient evidence to conclude that the mean volume is different than 18 oz.
There is sufficient evidence to conclude that the mean volume is different than 18 oz.
18 would be contained in a 95% confidence interval of the population mean.
18 would be contained in a 90% confidence interval of the population mean.
content.stem: Suppose that the p-value of the hypothesis test posed in the previous question (question 40) is 0.003. What conclusions can be made (use significance level 5%)?
content.why: The p-value (0.003) is less than the significance level (0.05), so there is sufficient evidence to reject the null hypothesis and conclude the mean volume differs from 18 oz; a 95% confidence interval would not contain 18. [VI.D.2]

content.stem: Speed bumps were installed in a neighborhood to slow traffic. After installation, the speeds after the last speed bump of a random sample of twenty cars were recorded. The mean speed was 24.50 mph and the standard deviation was 2.3 mph. The team wanted to determine if the average speed is less than 25 mph. What are the appropriate hypotheses for this hypothesis test?
content.why: This is a left-tailed test on a single population mean with unknown variance, assessing whether the mean is 25 mph or less: H0: μ=25 versus Ha: μ<25. [VI.D.2]

options: Reject H , and conclude that the proportion of patient falls equals 0.10.
Reject H , and conclude that the proportion of patient falls is more than 0.10.
Do not reject H ; conclude that the proportion of patient falls equals 0.10.
Do not reject H ; conclude that the proportion of patient falls is more than 0.10.
content.stem: A team investigated the number of patient falls in a hospital. Fifty-six patients were randomly selected. Out of the fifty-six patients, there were seven recorded patient falls. The hospital wanted to determine whether the proportion of patient falls was more than 10%. At the 5% significance level, what is your conclusion about this hypothesis test?
content.why: The sample proportion is 7/56=0.125. For H0: p=0.10 vs Ha: p>0.10 (right-tailed, α=0.05), z0 = (0.125-0.10)/√(0.10(0.90)/56) = 0.624, which is less than the critical value 1.645, so H0 is not rejected. [VI.D.2]

options: Yes, since 0 is not in the confidence interval.
Yes, since 0 is in the confidence interval.
No, since 0 is not in the confidence interval.
No, since 0 is in the confidence interval.
content.stem: Two methods for filling a bottle are being compared at a factory. The 90% confidence interval for the difference in volume for two independent random samples of the filling methods was found to be (–0.091, –0.049). Based on this confidence interval, is there evidence that the two filling methods are different?
content.why: The hypothesized value of 0 is not contained in the confidence interval (-0.091, -0.049), so there is evidence of a difference between the two population means. [VI.D.2]

content.stem: Corrective action and verification that nonconformities have been addressed are:
content.why: Actually taking corrective action when nonconformities have been identified is the one step in the process that is most often poorly executed. [II.D.3]

content.stem: An improvement project was done at a factory to decrease packaging time. The following data were collected before and after the improvement project: Before - sample mean = 3.52, sample variance = 2.34, sample size = 28. After - sample mean = 2.10, sample variance = 2.04, sample size = 25. A hypothesis test was performed with H0: μBefore - μAfter = 0 versus Ha: μBefore - μAfter > 0. What is the critical value for this hypothesis test (use α = 0.01)?
content.why: For H0: μBefore - μAfter = 0 vs Ha: μBefore - μAfter > 0 with α=0.01, the critical value is t0.01,51 = 2.402. [VI.D.2]

content.stem: Consider the scenario in the previous problem (question 45). The project team would like to determine whether the variance of packaging time has changed at the 10% significance level. What is the test statistic for the appropriate hypothesis test?

Two machines produce the same parts. A random sample of 1,250 parts from machine 1 has twenty-eight that are nonconforming, and a random sample of 1,175 parts from machine 2 has eighteen that are nonconforming. Find the 90% confidence interval for the difference between the proportions of nonconforming parts from machines 1 and 2.
A hypothesis test is performed at the 10% significance level. The power of the test is 0.80, or 80%. What is the type II error for this hypothesis test?
content.why: β = P(Type II error) = 1 - Power = 1 - 0.80 = 0.20. [VI.D.2]

content.stem: When the null hypothesis is not rejected when in fact the null hypothesis is false, what type of error has been made?
content.why: A Type II error occurs when H0 is not rejected even though it is actually false; a Type I error occurs when a true H0 is rejected. [VI.D.2]

content.stem: A team would like to compare the proportion of defective widgets produced by two machines. What distribution does the test statistic for this hypothesis test follow?
content.why: The two-sample proportion test statistic z0 = (p̂1-p̂2)/√[p̂(1-p̂)(1/n1+1/n2)] follows a standard normal distribution for sufficiently large sample sizes. [VI.D.2]

content.stem: The heart rates of twelve individuals were measured using two different pieces of equipment. A team would like to compare the measured heart rates of the two pieces of equipment. Which hypothesis test would be most appropriate?
content.why: A paired t-test is most appropriate because the same twelve individuals were measured twice, creating a strong relationship between the two measurements. [VI.D.3]

content.stem: The length of five components was measured by two inspectors (data shown below). Assuming the data follow a normal distribution, what is the test statistic for the appropriate hypothesis test for this scenario? Use α = 0.01. Component 1 2 3 4 5 Inspector A 10.2 9.8 10.1 10.3 10.4 Inspector B 10.0 9.9 10.3 10.0 10.3
content.why: This is a paired t-test since the same components were measured twice (once per inspector). Using differences d = A-B, d̄=0.06, sd=0.2074, t0 = 0.06/(0.2074/√5) = 0.65, which is less than the critical value 4.604, so H0 is not rejected. [VI.D.3]

content.stem: A team at a hospital did a project on medication errors. A random sample of medication errors yielded the following results: Type of error Number of errors Incorrect dose 32 Wrong dose 28 Incorrect form 45 Wrong amount 35 Total 140 The team would like to test the hypothesis at the 5% significance level that the medication errors occur with equal probabilities. What is the value of the test statistic for this hypothesis test?
content.why: This is a goodness-of-fit test for H0: p1=p2=p3=p4=0.25. With expected counts Ei=35, χ²0 = Σ(Oi-Ei)²/Ei = 4.514. [VI.D.4]

content.stem: What distribution does the test statistic used in the goodness-of-fit test follow?
content.why: The goodness-of-fit test statistic χ²0 = Σ(Oi-Ei)²/Ei follows a chi-square distribution with k-1 degrees of freedom, where k is the number of categories. [VI.D.4]

options: no time; it is not necessary for the auditor to explain this information to the auditee.
content.stem: The lead auditor must explain to the auditee the objectives of the audit as well as the methods that will be used. This is usually done during:
content.why: Generally, an audit is carried out in three steps: (1) pre-examination— the auditor explains the objectives of the audit, introduces team members to senior management, and so on; (2) a “suitability” audit is conducted— comparison of documented procedures to the reference standard selected; and (3) implementation of the quality system is examined in depth, which may involve recommending corrective measures. [II.D.3]

options: Reject H ; conclude that the three means are the same.
Reject H ; conclude that at least one mean is different than the others.
Do not reject H ; conclude that the three means are the same.
Do not reject H ; conclude that at least one mean is different than the others.
content.stem: A study was done to compare the elasticity of a polymer mortar during a compression test at three different strain rates. Below is the ANOVA table for the statistical analysis. What is your conclusion at the 5% significance level? Source dF SS MS F Strain rate 2 0.1614 0.0807 1.70 Error 12 0.5688 0.0474 Total 14 0.7302
content.why: Comparing the test statistic F0=1.70 to the critical value F0.05,2,12=19.41, since F0 < 19.41, H0 is not rejected and the three means are concluded to be the same. [VI.D.5]

content.stem: Which of the following is an assumption required for use and interpretation of a one-way ANOVA?
content.why: One-way ANOVA assumes observations follow a normal distribution, are independent, and have constant variance across treatments; paired data is not a requirement. [VI.D.5]

options: High levels of factor B tend to have smaller response values.
There is not an interaction effect between factors A and B.
There is an interaction effect between factors A and B.
Factors A and B do not have an effect on the response variable.
content.stem: A two-way ANOVA hypothesis test was used to test the effects of two factors, A and B, on a response variable. An interaction plot shows that as factor A moves across its levels, the two lines for factor B's low and high levels stay parallel, following identical up-and-down patterns (though the high level of factor B does sit at a higher response value than the low level). What conclusions can be made from this interaction plot?
content.why: An interaction plot with parallel lines across the levels of factor A (both factor B levels following identical up/down patterns) indicates no significant interaction between factors A and B, though high levels of factor B do correspond to higher response values. [VI.D.5]

options: Reject H0; conclude that type of parts produced and time of day are independent.
Reject H0; conclude that type of parts produced and time of day are not independent.
Do not reject H0; conclude that type of parts produced and time of day are independent.
Do not reject H0; conclude that type of parts produced and time of day are not independent.
content.stem: A contingency table cross-tabulates the number of conforming and nonconforming parts produced by time of day (day, evening, overnight shifts). A chi-square hypothesis test for independence between the type of part produced and time of day yields a test statistic of 19.071. What is the conclusion from this hypothesis test (use α = 0.05)?
content.why: With (r-1)(c-1)=2 degrees of freedom, the critical value χ²0.05,2 = 5.991. Since 19.071 > 5.991, H0 is rejected, and the type of part produced and time of day are concluded to not be independent. [VI.D.6]

content.stem: The fitted regression equation for two variables x and y is yˆ = 2.5x – 8. What is the slope of this equation?
content.why: The slope represents the change in y for a one-unit change in x; here that value is 2.5. [VI.E.1]

content.stem: A team wants to predict a person’s cholesterol based on their weight in pounds. The fitted regression equation is Cholesterol = 140 + 0.23 × Weight. What is the predicted cholesterol of a person who weighs 130 pounds?
content.why: Substituting Weight=130 into the equation: Cholesterol = 140 + 0.23(130) = 169.9. [VI.E.1]

content.stem: Paired data collected from a process are: (5.2, 26.7), (6.1, 27.5), (3.2, 24.9), (4.6, 25.5). What is the slope of the linear regression equation for these data?
content.why: Using Sxx=4.4475 and Sxy=4.105, the slope b1 = Sxy/Sxx = 4.105/4.4475 = 0.923, which rounds to 0.92 among the given choices. [VI.E.1]

content.stem: A study was done to predict people’s cholesterol by their weight. A sample of twenty-one people was collected, and the linear regression equation was found to be Cholesterol = 140 + 0.20 × Weight. The team would like to determine whether there is a significant linear relationship between weight and cholesterol. What is the appropriate alternative hypothesis for this statistical test?
content.why: The hypothesis test on the slope of the regression line uses H0: β1=0 versus Ha: β1≠0 (the intercept β0 is not the parameter of interest here). [VI.E.1]

content.stem: A scatterplot displays the relationship between two random variables: as x increases, y increases in a clear, tight, linear pattern. What is the correlation coefficient of these two variables?
content.why: The scatterplot shows y increasing as x increases, a positive linear relationship; a correlation coefficient close to +1 indicates a strong positive correlation, here 0.88. [VI.E.2]

content.stem: A scatterplot displays the relationship between two random variables: y traces a clear quadratic (curved, U-shaped) pattern as x increases, not a straight line. What is the correlation coefficient of these two variables?
content.why: The scatterplot shows a quadratic (curved), not linear, relationship between the variables, so despite the visible pattern the linear correlation coefficient r is 0. [VI.E.2]

content.stem: Who is responsible for the accuracy of the final audit report?
content.why: The lead auditor is responsible for the accuracy as well as the validity of the final report. [II.D.2]

content.stem: The fitted regression equation for two variables x and y is yˆ = –5x + 131. The coefficient of determination is 0.85, or 85%. What is the correlation coefficient?
content.why: The correlation coefficient r = ±√R² = ±√0.85 ≈ ±0.92; since the slope is negative (-5), the relationship is negative, so r = -0.92. [VI.E.2]

as the age of a car increases, the cost of the car tends to increase.
as the age of a car increases, the cost of the car tends to decrease.
the cost of a car is controlled by its age.
