content.why: A negative correlation coefficient indicates an inverse linear association: as the age of a car increases, its cost tends to decrease (though correlation does not imply causation). [VI.E.2]

content.stem: When the measurement for one sample tends to be dependent on the measure for the previous sample, these data are called:
content.why: Data are autocorrelated when a sample's value is affected by the value of the previous sample. [VI.E.3]

content.stem: Which of the following can help identify special cause variation in a process?
content.why: Statistical process control is the technique used to identify special cause variation; regression describes predictor-response relationships, histograms visualize data, and capability analysis checks whether a process meets requirements. [VI.F.1]

content.stem: A control chart was in control, but the operator adjusted the process anyway. What is this called?
content.why: Overcontrol (overadjustment) occurs when an operator adjusts a process in response to common cause variation even though the control chart did not signal out-of-control behavior. [VI.F.2]

options: To identify the source of special cause variation in a process
To adjust a process when it goes out of control
To help process operators recognize the presence of special causes of variation
content.stem: What is the principal purpose of control charts?
content.why: Control charts help operators recognize when special causes of variation are present; they do not identify the specific cause or automatically adjust the process. [VI.F.2]

options: Slight changes in customer arrivals to a store
content.stem: Which of the following events would be considered a source of special cause variation?
content.why: An incorrect machine setting is an unusual, correctable event and thus a source of special cause variation, unlike ambient temperature changes, measurement system variability, or normal customer-arrival fluctuations, which are common cause variation. [VI.F.2]

options: There is no difference between within-sample variability and between- sample variability.
content.stem: Which of the following statements about rational subgrouping is correct?
content.why: Rational subgrouping selects samples so that special cause variation is more likely to appear between samples while variability within samples is minimized. [VI.F.4]

content.stem: Which quality leader introduced the use of control charts to monitor a quality characteristic?
content.why: Walter A. Shewhart introduced the concept of control charts in the 1920s. [VI.F.5]

content.stem: What probability distribution is required to construct X and R control charts?
content.why: X̄, R, s, I, and MR control charts all require the underlying data to follow a normal distribution. [VI.F.5]

content.stem: Which of the following quality characteristics is an example of attribute data?
content.why: A defect is an attribute. Either the defect is present or it is not. A defect has no real measurement on a continuous scale. [III.A]

options: both the average and range were within the control limits.
neither the average nor range were within the control limits.
only the average was outside the control limits.
only the range was outside the control limits.
content.stem: An X̄ and R chart was prepared for an operation using twenty-five samples of seven pieces each. X̄ was found to be 24.8 and R̄ was 5.50. During production, a new sample of seven was taken and the pieces measured 25, 32, 35, 28, 27, 24, and 26. At the time this sample was taken, were both the average and range within the control limits?
content.why: For n=7, the new sample's x̄=28.14 and R=11. With x̄=24.8 and R̄=5.50, the X̄-chart limits are UCL=27.10, LCL=22.50, and the R-chart limits are UCL=10.58, LCL=0.418. Since 28.14 exceeds the X̄ UCL and 11 exceeds the R UCL, neither the average nor the range were within the control limits. [VI.F.5]

content.stem: The diameter of a steel rod is a quality characteristic of interest. Samples of size twelve will be selected in the subgroups. Which of the following control charts is preferred to monitor the process variability?
content.why: With variables data and a relatively large sample size (n=12), the sample standard deviation is a better estimator of process variability than the range, making an X̄ and s chart preferred over an X̄ and R chart. [VI.F.5]

options: both the average and standard deviation were within the control limits.
neither the average nor standard deviation were within the control limits.
only the average was outside the control limits.
only the standard deviation was outside the control limits.
content.stem: An X̄ and s chart was prepared for an operation using twenty-five samples with six pieces in each sample. X̄ was found to be 12.68 and s was 2.45. During production, a sample of six was taken and the pieces measured 11, 13, 14, 14, 10, and 12. At the time this sample was taken:
content.why: For the new sample, x̄=12.33 and s=1.633. With x̄=12.68 and s̄=2.45 (n=6), the X̄-chart limits are UCL=15.83, LCL=9.53, and the s-chart limits are UCL=4.83, LCL=0.07. Since both 12.33 and 1.633 fall within their respective limits, both the average and standard deviation were within the control limits. [VI.F.5]

content.stem: A company would like to monitor a continuous quality characteristic of a product. However, it is expensive to obtain the measurements of this quality characteristic. Which of the following control charts is most appropriate to monitor this process?
content.why: Since it's expensive to obtain measurements, subgroups of size 1 (individual observations) are used, making an I-MR chart the appropriate choice for this continuous quality characteristic. [VI.F.5]

content.stem: A hospital is monitoring the surgeries that result in surgical complications. The number of surgeries each month and those resulting in a complication were recorded. The number of surgeries each month can vary. Which of the following control charts is most appropriate to monitor this process?
content.why: Surgical complications are attribute data with a varying number of surgeries (opportunities) each month, so a p-chart is preferred over an np-chart, which requires a constant sample size. [VI.F.5]

options: the sample was within the control limits.
the sample was outside the control limits.
content.stem: A factory collected data on the number of nonconforming parts and constructed a p-chart. Fifteen samples of size 150 were collected. They determined that the average fraction of nonconforming parts was p̄ = 0.037. During production, a sample of 150 parts was taken, of which eleven were nonconforming. At the time this sample was taken:
content.why: With p̄=0.037 and n=150, the p-chart control limits are UCL=0.083 and LCL≈0 (the calculated negative LCL is set to 0). Since the new sample's p̂=11/150=0.073 falls within these limits, the sample is within the control limits. [VI.F.5]

content.stem: What is the upper control limit for a p-chart when the average daily production is 3575 units with an established fraction defective of 0.048?

A team at a factory would like to monitor the number of defects in a TV screen. Twenty-five samples of five TV screens are inspected. Which of the following control charts is most appropriate for this scenario?
content.why: TV screen defects are nonconformities (count data), which calls for a c-chart rather than an X̄/R chart (variables data) or a p-/np-chart (fraction nonconforming). [VI.F.5]

content.stem: A team at a factory is monitoring the average number of defects in TV screens. Thirty-five TV screens are randomly selected each day over a 25-day period. The average number of defects per TV screen was found to be u = 0.73. What is the upper control limit for a corresponding u-chart?
If a process is out of control, the probability that a single point on the X̄ chart will fall between plus two sigma and the upper control limit is:
content.why: Since the process is out of statistical control (unstable), the theoretical probability calculations for an in-control process no longer apply, so the actual probability is unknown. [VI.F.6]

options: mates with both ends of the limit gage (both “go” and “no-go”).
mates only with the “no-go” end of the gage.
mates with neither end of the limit gage.
mates with only the “go” end of the limit gage.
content.stem: A part will be inspected using a limit gage. An acceptable part is one that:
content.why: An acceptable part should only fit within the “go” end of the limit gage. If it passes on both ends, it is an unacceptable part. [III.A]

options: adjust the process when a point is not on target.
have a small average run length.
have a large average run length.
content.stem: If a process is in control, it is desirable to:
content.why: When a process is in control, a large average run length (the number of samples before a false out-of-control signal) is desirable, since operators should not adjust a stable, on-target process. [VI.F.6]

options: The process is out of control.
The process is operating within the specifications.
The process is operating outside the specifications.
content.stem: Consider an MR chart of a normally distributed process with UCL = 36.25, MR̄ = 11.09, and LCL = 0. One point on the chart falls above the upper control limit. What conclusions can be drawn from this control chart?
content.why: A point falls above the upper control limit on the MR chart, indicating the process is out of statistical control; a control chart says nothing about whether the process meets specification limits. [VI.F.6]

options: The process is out of control.
The process is operating within the specifications.
The process is operating outside the specifications.
content.stem: Consider a p-chart with UCL = 0.1151, p̄ = 0.0675, and LCL = 0.0199. Starting with the fourth sample, there is a run of sixteen consecutive points alternating up and down. What conclusions can be drawn from this control chart?
content.why: The chart shows a run of points alternating up and down, matching the out-of-control sensitizing rule for that pattern, so the process is out of statistical control; this control chart says nothing about whether it meets specification limits. [VI.F.6]

options: The process is out of control.
The process is operating within the specifications.
The process is operating outside the specifications.
content.stem: Consider an X̄ chart of a normally distributed process with UCL = 32.13, X̄̄ = 27.49, and LCL = 22.85. All plotted points fall within the control limits with no unusual patterns. What conclusions can be drawn from this control chart?
content.why: No unusual patterns or out-of-limits points appear on the chart, so the process is stable (in control); this says nothing about whether it meets specification limits. [VI.F.6]

content.stem: A manufacturing company received an order for a build-to-order product from a customer. The company would like to monitor the process; which of the following tools is most appropriate?
content.why: A build-to-order product does not have a long, continuous production run, so classical X̄/R charts aren't appropriate; short-run SPC (typically using standardized control charts) is needed instead. [VI.F.7]

options: Compare the actual capability to the desired capability.
Verify that the process is stable.
content.stem: What is the first step in a capability study?
content.why: The first step in a capability study is to verify the process is stable (free of special-cause variation), since capability measures aren't valid estimates otherwise. [VI.G.1]

content.stem: A team would like to determine whether a process is able to meet customer specifications. What quality tool should they use?
content.why: Capability analysis determines whether a process is able to meet requirements, often supplemented with histograms, probability plots, or stem-and-leaf plots. [VI.G.1]

content.stem: The dimension of a component has specifications 5.5 ± 0.25. The process data are normally distributed with mean 5.45 and standard deviation 0.085. What fraction of components will have this dimension outside the specification limits?
content.why: With USL=5.75, LSL=5.25, μ=5.45, σ=0.085: P(5.25<X<5.75) = P(-2.35<Z<3.53) ≈ 0.9904 within spec, so the fraction outside specification limits is 1-0.9904 = 0.0096. [VI.G.2]

content.stem: The diameter of a stainless-steel rod is an important quality characteristic. The rod has specifications 2.50 ± 0.05. Data from the process indicate the distribution is normally distributed, and an X̄ and R chart indicates the process is stable. The control charts used a sample of size seven and found that X̄ = 2.5014 and R̄ = 0.0568. What fraction of steel rods are within the specification limits?
content.why: With USL=2.55, LSL=2.45, x̄=2.5014, σ̂=R̄/d2=0.0568/2.704≈0.021: P(2.45<X<2.55) = P(-2.45<Z<2.31) ≈ 0.9825 of rods fall within the specification limits. [VI.G.2]

options: Specification limits are determined externally and do not have a generic formula.
content.stem: Which of the following is the correct formula to find the specification limits of a quality characteristic?
content.why: Specification limits are determined externally (by management, engineers, or customers) and have no generic statistical formula; they are unrelated to control limits. [VI.G.2]

content.stem: A system has two components in parallel, each with a reliability of 0.95. The system reliability is approximately:
content.why: For components in parallel, each with reliability of p, the system reliability is given by Rs(t) = 1 – (1 – p)2 = 1 – (1 – 0.95)2 = 0.9975. [III.E.2]

content.stem: A stable, normally distributed process has specifications 21.35 ± 4.50. A sample from the process had a mean X̄ = 20.98 and standard deviation σ = 1.10. Find Cₚ and Cₚₖ.
A stable process has specifications 14 ± 5. The process is normally distributed with mean 13 and standard deviation 1.5. Is this process considered capable?
content.why: Since the process is not centered, Cpk is the appropriate metric: Cpk = min[(19-13)/3(1.5), (13-9)/3(1.5)] = min(1.33, 0.89) = 0.89, which is less than 1, so the process is not capable. [VI.G.3]

content.stem: The diameter of a stainless-steel rod is an important quality characteristic. The rod has specifications 2.50 ± 0.05. Data from the process indicate the distribution is normally distributed, and an X̄ and R chart indicates the process is stable. The control charts used a sample of size seven and found that X̄ = 2.5014 and R̄ = 0.0568. What is the capability of this process?
content.why: With USL=2.55, LSL=2.45, σ̂=R̄/d2≈0.021: since the process is centered, Cp = (USL-LSL)/6σ = 0.10/0.126 ≈ 0.79, which is less than 1, so the process is not capable. [VI.G.3]

content.stem: Which of the following metrics is recommended to evaluate process capability when the process is not in statistical control?
content.why: Pp (process performance) is the recommended metric when a process is not in statistical control, unlike Cp/Cpk, which assume a stable, in-control process. [VI.G.4]

content.stem: A textile company is designing an experiment to test the effects of temperature, pressure, and time on the tensile properties of a fiber composite. Each of these three factors will be run at a high and low level. A full-factorial design is used with four replicates per run. How many treatment combinations are in this experiment?
content.why: A treatment combination is a unique combination of factor levels applied to an experimental unit; with three factors at two levels each, there are 2×2×2=8 treatment combinations. [VI.H.1]

content.stem: A textile company is designing an experiment to test the effects of temperature, pressure, and time on the tensile properties of a fiber composite. Each of these three factors will be run at a high and low level. A full-factorial design is used with four replicates per run. How many factors are in this experiment?
content.why: The experiment tests three factors (temperature, pressure, and time), each at two levels, with four replicates per treatment combination. [VI.H.1]

content.stem: A textile company is designing an experiment to test the effects of temperature, pressure, and time on the tensile properties of a fiber composite. Each of these three factors will be run at a high and low level. A full-factorial design is used with four replicates per run. Variation observed in the readings of the replicates for each treatment combination is referred to as what?
content.why: Experimental error is the variation observed among the replicate readings for a given treatment combination; fewer replicates make this error estimate less accurate. [VI.H.1]

options: State the objective of the experiment.
content.stem: What is the first step in designing a successful experiment?
content.why: The first step in designing an experiment is to clearly state its objective, which guides the selection of factors, responses, measurement method, and design. [VI.H.2]

content.stem: What technique in experimental design will reduce the effect of uncontrolled variables that are not part of the experiment but might affect the response variable?
content.why: Randomization orders the treatment combinations randomly to reduce the effect of uncontrolled nuisance factors that cannot be controlled during the experiment. [VI.H.3]

content.stem: An experiment is being conducted in a factory. Each experimental run takes several hours, so the experiment will last several days. What design technique would help in this experiment?
content.why: Since the experiment spans several days, blocking on day removes any day-to-day effect from influencing the response. [VI.H.3]

content.stem: Which concept is used to identify drivers of quality based on the Voice of the Customer?
content.why: A Critical to Quality Tree is used to identify the drivers of quality based on the Voice of the Customer. [III.B.1]

content.stem: An experiment is being conducted on the yield of a substance. Two factors are believed to have an effect on the yield. What type of design would be appropriate for this experiment?
content.why: With two factors of interest and no blocking variables, a factorial design is appropriate. [VI.H.4]

content.stem: Consider the following results of a 23 full-factorial design. Assuming normality and equal variance assumptions are valid, which terms have a significant effect on the response variable? Source df SS MS F p-value A 1 35.03 35.03 264.38 0.000 B 1 30.54 30.54 230.49 0.000 C 1 0.10 0.10 0.75 0.400 AB 1 2.98 2.98 22.49 0.001 AC 1 0.02 0.02 0.15 0.693 BC 1 0.03 0.03 0.23 0.646 ABC 1 0.002 0.002 0.15 0.902 Error 8 1.06 0.1325 Total 15 69.76
content.why: The ANOVA table shows very small p-values (0.000-0.001) only for main effects A and B and their AB interaction, so only A, B, and AB have a significant effect on the response. [VI.H.4]

content.stem: Which of the following graphical tools can help assess the assumption of independence when analyzing the results of a full-factorial design?
content.why: If run order is known, a run chart of the responses or residuals can reveal patterns that indicate a lack of independence. [VI.H.4]

content.stem: A 24 full-factorial experiment is conducted with a single replicate. If all main effects and interactions are included in the model, how many degrees of freedom does the error term have?
content.why: A single-replicate 2^4 design has 2^4-1=15 total degrees of freedom, all consumed by the four main effects, six two-way, four three-way, and one four-way interaction, leaving none for error. [VI.H.4]

content.stem: An experiment has eight factors at two levels each. The experiment has 128 runs. What is the experimental design called?
content.why: 128 runs is 2^8/2 = 2^7, i.e. half of the full 2^8=256 run design, making this a half-fractional factorial design. [VI.H.5]

options: all main effects and two-factor interactions are estimable.
content.stem: An advantage of using a full-factorial design over a fractional factorial design is that:
content.why: A full-factorial design allows all main effects and all two-factor interactions to be fully estimable, unlike a fractional factorial design, which requires fewer runs but confounds some effects. [VI.H.5]

content.stem: In a resolution IV fractional factorial experiment, main effects are confounded with:
content.why: In a resolution IV design, main effects are confounded with three-factor and higher interactions (and two-factor interactions with other two-factor interactions). [VI.H.5]

options: B is not aliased with other effects.
content.stem: Consider an experiment with five factors each at two levels. Using the defining relation I = ABD = ACE = BCDE, with which effects is main effect B aliased?
content.why: Using the defining relation I=ABD=ACE=BCDE, multiplying B by each term gives B×ABD=AD, B×ACE=ABCE, and B×BCDE=CDE, so main effect B is aliased with AD and CDE (among the given choices). [VI.H.6]

content.stem: An experiment is being conducted to find the optimal ingredients for a cake mix. The experimenters want the taste of the cake to be unaffected by small variations in oven temperature in the customers’ homes. This is a problem of:
content.why: Robustness means resistance to variation in an uncontrollable factor; since oven temperature in customers' homes can't be controlled, the cake mix should be designed to be robust to it. [VI.H.6]

options: There is no robust design problem for this experiment.
It may be possible to find settings of the ingredients that are robust to the oven temperature.
The oven temperature does not have an effect on the taste of the cake.
The three ingredients are uncontrollable factors in this experiment.
content.stem: A team conducted an experiment to determine the optimal amount of three ingredients in a cake to maximize the taste. Two noise factors (oven temperature and baking time) were also included. A crossed-array design was used. The analysis indicated that there was a significant interaction between one of the ingredients and the oven temperature. Which of the following statements is true?
content.why: A significant interaction between an ingredient (a controllable factor) and oven temperature (a noise factor) suggests it may be possible to choose ingredient settings that make the response robust to oven temperature variation. [VI.H.6]

content.stem: Quality defined as “fitness for use” is attributed to:
content.why: Juran believed that a product is fit for use if it meets customer expectations. [I.A.2]

content.stem: Consider the product/process development life cycle. The phase in which the product or process is in the hands of the customer for use is the:
content.why: The post-production phase of the development life cycle includes release of the product/process to the customer for its intended use or function. Normal wear and maintenance occur in this phase as well. [III.B.1]

options: Fourth layer/tier: quality records/results of implementation
content.stem: Consider the four layers or tiers of a quality manual. Which layer describes the company’s commitments, what it stands for, and objectives for quality?
content.why: The policy statement is the first layer in the manual because it not only provides information about the company’s commitment, but policy statements are often provided for each of the applicable standards. [II.B.1]

content.stem: A quality audit is to be conducted within a particular company. The company has hired an independent contractor to conduct the audit. The contractor is an example of:
content.why: An independent contractor not associated with the auditee would be considered an external quality auditor. [II.D.2]

options: to provide consistency in terms, vocabulary, and requirements.
because industry-specific standards were simply carbon copies of national standards.
because some organizations were more profitable than others.
content.stem: The need for an international standard like ISO 9000 arose:
content.why: International standards are necessary because they provide a consistent way for interpreting terms, vocabulary, and requirements regardless of language or location of the reader (different languages interpreting information differently was a key problem with standards from different countries and in different languages). [II.C]

content.stem: When there is no control in place to address a significant risk, or the control is insufficient for that particular risk, there is a:
content.why: When the control in place is not adequate for the risk, or no control has been put in place for a significant risk, this is called a gap or control gap. [VII.C.1]

content.stem: A risk manager is focused on reducing the risk of outpatient laparoscopic surgery. After risk mitigations, the number of infections post-surgery has been reduced from 5% to 0.05% over six months but has not been able to be reduced below 0.05% despite further efforts. This level of risk of infection after all possible and imaginable mitigations are applied is known as:
content.why: The risk remaining after all possible mitigations have been applied and cannot be reduced further is the risk that cannot be treated. In this case, since every possible mitigation has already been applied, residual risk equals inherent untreatable risk. [VII.C.5]

options: A detailed description of the process
The machine number used in the process
Steps for appropriate disposition of suspect material/products
content.stem: Which of the following can you typically find in a reaction plan for a process?
content.why: A reaction plan typically contains four elements: containment, diagnosis, verification, and disposition, including specific directions for how to dispose of contained material when a problem is detected in the process (scrap, rework, sort, use as-is, or return to vendor). [VII.C.1]

options: Do not drive at all and so do not pick up groceries until snow melts.
Put on snow tires for better traction.
Pay your neighbor with a truck to drive and buy groceries for you.
Drive in snow and hope for the best.
content.stem: When driving in the snow and slippery black ice to pick up groceries, which of the following risk treatment options qualifies as risk mitigation?
content.why: Putting on snow tires is risk mitigation. Not driving at all is risk avoidance. Paying the neighbor to drive is risk transfer. Driving and hoping for the best is risk acceptance. [VII.C.3]

options: Frequency of risk tracking review and reporting
content.stem: Which of the following should be contained in a risk management plan?
content.why: Of the listed options, only the frequency of risk tracking review and reporting can be stated at the time of risk management planning; the others (a completed FMEA, audit results, monitoring results) are outputs produced later, during risk execution. [VII.B.1]

options: evaluation/testing (e.g., human factors/usability, verification, validation, clinical investigations).
supplier evaluation criteria (e.g., self-assessment forms, audits, etc.).
content.stem: When assessing process risk through audits, a risk-based audit approach for a design change should include a review of:
content.why: A risk-based audit approach for a design change should include a review of the level of evaluation/testing (e.g., human factors/usability, verification, validation, clinical investigations), along with related regulatory requirements and the level of change approval required. [VII.C.3]

content.stem: Maintaining risk at or below an acceptable level is part of:
content.why: Maintaining risk at or below an acceptable level is a core purpose of risk control. [VII.C.1]

content.stem: Which of the following would be a Critical to Quality characteristic?
content.why: A Critical to Quality characteristic is needed to achieve the driver and may consist of a specification such as length 18.0 to 18.2 cm. [III.B.1]

options: To determine the level of impact
To help fill out a risk register/FMEA
content.stem: What is the purpose of a rating scale for consequence or severity?
content.why: A rating scale for consequence or severity exists to distinguish and quantify the level of impact so that consequences across different risks can be compared and evaluated. [VII.B.2]

options: it cannot be used to identify combinations of failure modes, only single failure modes.
it only uses binary data such as failure/no failure.
it is too complicated, since it does not require the user to know anything about the process or product.
it cannot be used in certain industries.
content.stem: A fault tree analysis (FTA) is a useful tool for prioritizing risks. One of the drawbacks or limitations of the FTA is:
content.why: Fault tree analysis (FTA) only uses binary data (failure/no failure), which is often considered a limitation of the technique, although the method remains very effective for failure analysis. [VII.B.2]

content.stem: Last month, a local company reported the following quality costs: Incoming inspection $60,000; Design support $12,000; Field trials $110,000; Returns by customers $40,000. What is the total appraisal cost for last month?
content.why: The only appraisal cost among the four listed is incoming inspection ($60,000); design support and field trials are prevention costs, and returns by customers is an external failure cost. [II.E]

content.stem: Teams that are formed for the purpose of elevating an existing process or developing a new one are:
content.why: Process improvement teams should be cross-functional, consisting of people from many different departments or areas within the company (and possibly externally, such as customers and suppliers). [I.D.4]

content.stem: What quality tool would be good for conducting a needs analysis when considering a new training program?
content.why: Using a QFD (quality function deployment) to identify the needs of a training program can provide a more focused approach to the program's design and delivery. [II.F.15]

options: rating the supplier’s financial, manufacturing, and quality systems.
rating the supplier’s list of other customers.
content.stem: An organization desires to begin rating the capabilities of one of its new suppliers. The process for rating this supplier must include:
content.why: The supplier's physical location may be of some interest but is not necessarily part of the rating process. Evaluating a supplier's ethnicity would be both unethical and illegal. [I.H.8]

content.stem: A safe way to avoid ASQ Code of Ethics violations is to be consistently:
content.why: Section A of the ASQ Code of Ethics, "Act with Integrity and Honesty," includes the statement, "Be truthful and transparent in all professional interactions and activities." [I.C]

options: individuals begin to shift from personal concerns to the needs of the team.
the team’s mission is clarified and specific roles are identified.
team members still think and act as individuals instead of impacting as a team.
the team has matured and is working in the best interest of the team and team goals.
content.stem: Common development stages that teams often progress through are known as forming, storming, norming, and performing. In the “norming” stage:
content.why: In the norming phase, interpersonal conflicts have less impact on team dynamics and work, and individuals begin shifting from personal concerns to the needs of the team. [I.D]

content.stem: The acronym NPV stands for:
content.why: NPV is short for net present value. [I.B.2.c]

content.stem: According to the ASQ Code of Ethics, confidential information should be:
content.why: The ASQ Code of Ethics states members should "ensure the protection and integrity of confidential information." [I.C]

content.stem: Consider the product/process development life cycle. The phase in which all possible
content.why: In the concept phase, all possible solutions are explored. Solutions that are not feasible are eliminated. [III.B.1]

content.stem: Philip Crosby is credited with which definition of quality?
content.why: Crosby is credited with "conformance to specification." Juran is credited with "fitness for use," and Genichi Taguchi is credited with "uniformity around a target value." "Defect-free product" was never a formal definition of quality. [I.A.1]

content.stem: Active listening by team members is an important skill that is not often easy to attain with new teams. Which of the following is one of the dimensions of active listening?
content.why: Confirming is the only option here that counts as active listening; listening to music and simultaneous speaking both hinder communication, and being defensive on a team quickly defeats the purpose of teamwork. [I.F]

options: Obtaining a free conference pass as a presenter
Expensing the conference at work as a training event
Paying for the conference from personal funds
Attending the conference using someone else’s badge
content.stem: Which of the following actions would result in an ASQ Code of Ethics violation?
content.why: The ASQ Code of Ethics requires members to accurately represent their own professional qualifications and to uphold the integrity, honor, and dignity of the profession; attending a conference under someone else's badge misrepresents identity and credentials. [I.C]

content.stem: In one year, a company spent more than $500,000 on warranty issues. This cost would be categorized as:
content.why: Warranty costs fall under external failure costs. [II.E]

options: individuals begin to shift from personal concerns to needs of the team.
the team’s mission is clarified and specific roles are identified.
team members still think and act as individuals instead of impacting as a team.
team has matured and is working in the best interest of the team and team goals.
content.stem: Common development stages teams often progress through are known as forming, storming, norming, and performing. In the forming stage:
content.why: In the forming phase, an important task is developing and clarifying the team's mission and identifying specific roles. [I.D]

options: Institute barriers that stand between the hourly worker and his right to pride of workmanship.
Institute modern methods of training on the job.
15% of quality problems are due to the system.
85% of quality problems are due to management.
content.stem: Which of the following is one of Deming’s fourteen points?
content.why: Instituting modern training methods was necessary to introduce new methods to the workforce; the other listed options misstate Deming's points (which call for removing barriers to pride of workmanship, and attribute roughly 85% of quality problems to management/the system rather than 15%). [I.A.1]

content.stem: A group of operators in a semiconductor factory have an idea to improve their workflow. However, upper management has been reluctant to explore this idea. How might this group of operators classify this response?
content.why: This is an example of waste due to lost creativity. Management should encourage a quality team to investigate the proposed idea, which could lead to process improvements and also boost employee morale. [V.D]

options: people who are being asked for advice.
content.stem: According to RACI definitions, examples of people in the Informed role are:
content.why: Informed people are not those actually performing the project tasks, but they are kept informed so they can help remove roadblocks and ensure financial and resource support. [I.B.2.d]

content.stem: The Malcolm Baldrige National Quality Award emphasizes:
content.why: The Malcolm Baldrige National Quality Award emphasizes results; it is not given for specific products or services but to reward achievements in quality and performance excellence. [II.C]

content.stem: Last month, a local company reported the following quality costs: Incoming inspection $60,000; Design support $12,000; Field trials $110,000; Returns by customers $40,000. What is the total prevention cost for last month?
content.why: Design support and field trials both fall under prevention costs: $12,000 + $110,000 = $122,000. [II.E]

options: Mistakes as in defects per million opportunities
content.stem: Which of the following is an example of the Voice of the Customer in a Critical to Quality Tree?
content.why: An insurance policy is what the customer asks for. Voice of the Customer may be vague and not measurable, unlike the Critical to Quality characteristics. [III.B.1]

content.stem: A system improvement program based primarily on minimizing variability is called:
content.why: Lean deals with eliminating waste. Lean-Six Sigma focuses on eliminating waste and minimizing variability. [I.A.1]

options: To organize and summarize ideas generated about a particular problem or issue
To communicate hierarchical relationships between events
To assess a process implementation plan during the initial phases of operations
To visualize and identify causal relationships of a problem or situation
content.stem: What is the main purpose of an interrelationship digraph?
content.why: Interrelationship digraphs provide a means to identify sequential or cause- and-effect relationships of a problem or situation. Affinity diagrams are used to organize general thoughts and ideas about a topic. Tree diagrams are used to visualize hierarchical events of a process, and process decision program charts (PDPCs) help to evaluate a process implementation plan at a high level. [V.B]

options: Wait for the decision of the Material Review Board (MRB).
content.stem: A defect was discovered in a laptop battery. How should the company handle the disposition of this defective battery?
content.why: When a product defect is discovered, the material review board (MRB) determines what corrective actions to take. [IV.B.4]

content.stem: Which phase of the corrective action cycle helps prevent problem backsliding?
content.why: In the problem identification phase, the team identifies sources for improvement and develops a clear problem statement. In the correction phase, the team develops feasible solutions to the problem and recommends the best choice to implement. In the recurrence control phase, the team standardizes the solution to ensure that the problem does not reoccur and prevent backsliding. Finally, in the effectiveness assessment phase, the team continues monitoring the process to identify additional opportunities for improvement. [V.E]

content.stem: Which quality leader proposed using signal-to-noise ratios to improve robustness of a process?
content.why: Genichi Taguchi proposed signal-to-noise (S/N) ratios to optimize a response variable while minimizing its variability, with different S/N formulas depending on whether the goal is to maximize the response, minimize it, or hit a target value. [VI.H.5]

content.stem: Which lean tool results in reductions in process variation, more consistent products, and simplified downstream activities?
content.why: Standardized work means that each activity is done the same way every time. Because each employee performs the activities the same way, having standardized work in practice will help reduce process variation and provide more consistent (and likely better) products. Standardized work can also help simplify activities downstream. [V.D]

content.stem: A quality project team is investigating the root cause of variation in a fish tank manufacturing facility. In what stage of the Define-Measure-Analyze-Improve- Control (DMAIC) process is this team?
content.why: DMAIC is made up of five phases used in an improvement process: define, measure, analyze, improve, and control. In the analyze phase, the team has already clearly defined the problem and related metrics, and has measured the performance of the process. The team now investigates the root cause of variation in the process or poor performance. [V.C]

content.stem: A system improvement program based on both eliminating waste and reducing variation is called:
content.why: Lean deals with eliminating waste. Six Sigma focuses on reducing variation. Lean-Six Sigma focuses on eliminating waste and minimizing variability. [I.A.1]

content.stem: In which phase of the corrective action cycle does a team develop feasible solutions to improve a process?
content.why: In the problem identification phase, the team identifies sources for improvement and develops a clear problem statement. In the correction phase, the team develops feasible solutions to the problem and recommends the best choice to implement. In the recurrence control phase, the team standardizes the solution to ensure that the problem does not reoccur. Finally, in the effectiveness assessment phase, the team continues monitoring the process to identify additional opportunities for improvement. [V.E]

content.stem: Which of the following is the activity that may be part of the data transform phase?
content.why: The data transform phase's main goal is preparing data to fit the parameters of another system, through steps like sorting and filtering out irrelevant items, de-duplicating and cleansing, translating and converting, encrypting sensitive information, or splitting or joining tables.

content.stem: A tool that is useful for converting customer needs into design concepts is:
content.why: QFD, which uses the "house of quality," is helpful in turning customer needs into product characteristics or design concepts. [III.B.2]

content.stem: A company maintained a large stock of supplies in its warehouse. As a result, a sizeable portion of the materials had degraded by the time that they were required. As what type of waste would the company classify this event?
content.why: This is an example of waste due to inventory. The company has more inventory in storage than is necessary. As a result, it must pay to store these materials, which have no value to the customer. In addition, the company’s high inventory also leads to additional losses when some of the products degrade before use. [V.D]

content.stem: What item below is a benefit of a 5 Why Analysis?
content.why: The purpose of a 5 Why root cause analysis is to identify the system or process that caused the issue, which helps prevent the problem from recurring; fast reaction time and improved communication are also benefits. [V.E]

content.stem: A company’s shipment of textbooks to customers became illegible during the printing process due to an ink malfunction. The company must replace each customer’s order. How would the company classify this defect?
content.why: While the illegible textbooks will not cause injury, they do represent a large economic loss, as the company must replace all of the defective books. The company would classify this as a serious defect. [IV.B.3]

content.stem: When would inspection be most likely to be considered a value-added activity?
content.why: There are situations where inspection may be considered non-value-added and other situations where it is considered value-added. Inspection of low-cost items, for example, tends to be considered a non-value-added activity. However, inspection of a higher-risk product, or one that is required to be tested by law, could be considered value-added. [V.D]

content.stem: Which of the following represents ideal conditions for OEE?
content.why: As stated in The ASQ Certified Quality Engineer Handbook, Fifth Edition, Seiichi Nakajima noted the ideal OEE condition of >90% availability, >95% efficiency, and >99% quality based on his experience. The ideal OEE is therefore documented by Nakajima as greater than or equal to 85%. [V.D]

content.stem: An online ordering form for a company will not go through unless the customer has completely filled out all the shipping information and their address is automatically checked as a valid address. This is an example of:
content.why: This is an example of error-proofing, also known as poka-yoke. The order will not be processed unless there is complete shipping information and the address has been verified as valid. These extra steps should help reduce errors in shipping. [V.F]

content.stem: What quality management tool can be used to discover a hierarchical relationship between events that lead to a failure in a process or to map out the events that lead to a particular outcome?
content.why: A tree diagram can take on several shapes. A fault tree is used to discover a hierarchical relationship between events that led to a failure in a process. Similarly, an event tree defines the relationship between events that lead to a given outcome. A concept fan is used during the creative process of finding alternate concepts that achieve the same requirements as a process or product. [V.B]

content.stem: The temperature of a chicken entrée prepared in a restaurant was collected in a performance improvement project. The team would like to compare the distribution of the data collected to the target temperature of 165°F. Which of the following quality control tools is most appropriate to use?
content.why: Histograms are used to understand the shape, spread, and distribution of a data set, making them useful for comparing data against a target value or specification limit. Scatter diagrams depict the relationship between two continuous variables, Pareto charts identify the most common defects or occurrences, and control charts identify out-of-control behavior. [V.A]

content.stem: In a lean system, what is another name for waste?
content.why: Muda is another name for waste. Kaizen is a performance improvement methodology that emphasizes incremental changes to improve a system. Kanban is a visual system that helps to manage the procedure for resupplying tools, components, and so on, in the workplace. Seiton is one of the five S’s and means proper arrangement. [V.D]

content.stem: Employees at a pharmacy continuously look for ways to make their jobs easier. They color-coded cabinets to better identify materials. They placed check sheets near supplies to keep track of when they needed to be replaced. Finally, they created a document for employees to use to avoid rework when they called customers. Which of the following improvement methods have these employees been using?
content.why: The employees have made small, incremental improvements to their processes at the pharmacy. These are kaizen activities: incremental changes that improve a process without requiring expensive technology or equipment. [V.C]

content.stem: A planning technique that translates customer requirements into technical requirements is:
content.why: QFD is a powerful tool for incorporating the voice of the customer and identifying the necessary technical requirements that will be necessary to satisfy customer requirements. [III.B.2]

content.stem: Which of the following lean tools for helping to reduce changeover times has been attributed to Shigeo Shingo and the Toyota Production System?
content.why: Single minute exchange of die (SMED) is a method for reducing changeover times of machines. It has been attributed to Shigeo Shingo and his Toyota Production System. The goal of implementing SMED is to reduce the time required to switch a machine or assembly to a different product. [V.D]

content.stem: A hospital denotes different areas by color (for example, blue, pink, green). In each area, room signs and floors are painted with their designated color. This is an example of:
content.why: The floors and room signs match the designated color of each hospital area. This is an example of visual control -- the added visual cues help patients and employees know where they are in a complicated building. [V.D]

options: To visualize the relationship between two sets of factors
To assess a process implementation plan during the initial phases of operations
To manage the schedule of a complex process
To evaluate differing options based on a set of criteria
content.stem: What is the primary purpose of a process decision program chart?
content.why: Process decision program charts are primarily used to help evaluate a process implementation. They allow a team to assess the implementation plan, identify potential deviations, or develop contingency plans. Activity network diagrams are primarily used to help manage the schedule and timing of a project or set of actions. [V.B]

content.stem: A hospital is trying to improve patient flow in its emergency department by tracking patients. Which of the following would help most in this endeavor?
content.why: Radio-frequency identification (RFID) is an effective method for identification and tracking. In healthcare, RFID has been used effectively in patient care by tracking patient movements while they are hospitalized. [IV.B.1]

content.stem: Which of the following improvement methodologies provides a framework to iteratively improve a process?
content.why: The plan-do-check-act (PDCA) cycle, also called the Shewhart or Deming (PDSA) cycle, provides a four-step, iterative procedure for implementing process changes. TQM is an organization-wide quality program, TOC focuses on a process's weakest link, and reengineering involves redesigning a process for large quality improvements. [V.C]

content.stem: An online store is reviewing causes for its large number of customer returns. A Pareto chart revealed that the most frequent reason for returns cited by customers was “Item not what I ordered.” How would the store classify this type of waste?
content.why: This is an example of waste due to defect correction. The most frequent cause for returns was because the company shipped the wrong item to the customer. The company therefore had to perform rework—process the return, find the correct item, and pay for shipping. [V.D]

content.stem: The concept that it is ideal to move as many activities from external to internal as possible to reduce changeover times can be attributed to:
content.why: Internal activities are defined as activities performed while the machine is down. External activities are defined as actions done in preparation for a machine changeover. Shingo recommended moving as many internal activities to external activities as possible. [V.D]

content.stem: In a gage R&R study, the standard deviation associated with repeatability was found to be 0.9214, and the standard deviation associated with reproducibility was found to be 0.5873. What is the standard deviation associated with measurement error?
content.why: The variance associated with measurement error is the sum of the repeatability and reproducibility variances: σ²Measurement error = σ²Repeatability + σ²Reproducibility = 0.9214² + 0.5873² = 1.0927, so the standard deviation is √1.0927 ≈ 1.0453 (rounding differences aside, matching option b). Standard deviation is not additive; variance is. [IV.F]

content.stem: Which of the following involves verifying that the process parameters in place will result in a product or process that meets all requirements under all possible manufacturing conditions?
content.why: The goal is to identify limits and action levels that will result in a process or product that meets all of its requirements. [III.D]

options: No; the part should be rejected.
Yes; the part should be rejected.
No; the part should be accepted.
Yes; the part should be accepted.
content.stem: A part was inspected using a go/no-go gage. The part mated with both ends of the gage. Did the part pass inspection?
content.why: A part passes inspection with a go/no-go gage if it mates with the "go" end and does not mate with the "no-go" end. Since this part mated with both ends, it did not pass the no-go inspection and should be rejected. [IV.D.1]

content.stem: Which of the following methodologies may include components such as design for cost, manufacturability, or reliability?
content.why: Design for Six Sigma is an approach used to eliminate problems before they occur. Design for X is a subset of design for Six Sigma. [III.B.2]

options: The gage is capable of distinguishing between parts.
There is a significant difference between operators.
The chart reflects variability related to gage reproducibility.
The gage is not capable of distinguishing between parts.
content.stem: An X̄ chart by operator from a gage R&R study (ten parts, two operators, three replicates) shows UCL = 33.75, X̄̄ = 30.07, LCL = 26.38, with most of the plotted points falling within these control limits. What conclusions may be drawn from this control chart?
content.why: An X̄ chart by operator from a gage R&R study (ten parts, two operators, three replicates) shows UCL = 33.75, X̄̄ = 30.07, LCL = 26.38, with most of the plotted points falling within these control limits. The X̄ control chart reflects between-part variability; if the gage were capable of distinguishing between parts, most points would fall outside the control limits. Since most points here fall within the limits instead, this indicates the gage cannot distinguish between parts.

content.stem: A lot of size 100 is to be inspected using ANSI/ASQ Z1.4-2003 (R2018). The acceptance quality limit (AQL) is 1.5%. What is the required sample size for a single sampling plan (normal, level II inspection)?
content.why: Given that the lot size is 100, the sample size code letter from the ANSI/ASQ Z1.4-2003 (R2018) sampling tables for normal, level II sampling is F. Using Table II-A and following the down arrow, sampling plan G is referred to and the required sample size is then n = 32. [IV.C.2]
