has a low probability of accepting lots with good quality.
content.stem: A company compares two competing sampling plans using their OC (operating characteristic) curves plotted against lot percentage defective. Curve A (dashed) maintains a high probability of accepting the lot even at large percentages nonconforming, while Curve B (solid) drops off more steeply as percentage defective increases. Compared to Curve B, Curve A:
content.why: A company compares two competing sampling plans using their OC (operating characteristic) curves plotted against lot percentage defective. Curve A (dashed) maintains a high probability of accepting the lot even at large percentages nonconforming, while Curve B (solid) drops off more steeply. Compared to Curve B, Curve A:

content.stem: Consider a sampling plan with n = 80 and c = 2. Given that the percentage nonconforming is 0.025 and a Poisson distribution is appropriate, what is the probability of accepting the lot?
content.why: Using the Poisson approximation to the binomial, with np = 80(0.025) = 2 as the Poisson mean: Pa = P(d≤2) = Σ² (2)^d e^-2 / d! = 0.677. [IV.C.1]

content.stem: Which of the following components of measurement systems contributes to the precision?
content.why: The precision of a measurement system consists of repeatability and reproducibility. Gage bias, linearity, and stability describe the accuracy of a measurement system. [IV.F]

options: calibration of measuring equipment is critical.
consistent measuring devices provide confidence in the accuracy of the process.
little consideration is often given to a test operator’s contribution to measurement error.
random errors in measurement must be taken into account.
content.stem: Measurement assurance is an important concept in metrology because:
content.why: Measurement assurance includes information on the contribution of error from technicians and a lab's own procedures; calibration alone typically gets the focus, with little consideration given to errors from operators or the environment. [IV.E]

content.stem: Increasing the readability of a measuring instrument will lead to increased:
content.why: Readability is defined as the ease of reading the instrument scale while measuring some component. The readability of the equipment, however, will not necessarily result in more accurate results in measurement. [IV.E]

content.stem: Evaluation of the capability of equipment, selection of measurement standards, and detailed procedures to carry out measurements are key components of:
content.why: Typical calibration control systems include the following procedures: evaluation of equipment to determine its capability, identification of calibration requirements, selection of standards to perform calibration, selection of the methods to carry out the measurements for the calibration, and more. [IV.E]

content.stem: The inside dimensions of a part are inspected for conformance to product specifications. Which of the following measuring tools is most appropriate to inspect its dimensions?
content.why: Plug gages are typically used to assess conformance of inside dimensions of a part. Ring and snap gages are used to assess outside dimensions. Splines are typically used to check special features. Micrometers are used for linear measurements. [IV.D.1]

content.stem: A company produces a part continuously. Which type of OC curve is appropriate for the proposed sampling plan?
content.why: Type B OC curves are used to evaluate a sampling plan for a continuous process (constructed with a binomial or Poisson distribution). Type A OC curves are used on a lot-by-lot basis for a finite lot from a continuous process. [IV.C.1]

options: a cross-functional team including quality, manufacturing, and suppliers, and so on.
content.stem: Design reviews should be conducted by
content.why: Because of the complexity of design reviews, a cross-functional team consisting of many different personnel should conduct the review. The team should include, but not be limited to, quality personnel, manufacturing, suppliers, customers, and so on. [III.B.3]

content.stem: In a gage R&R study, the variance associated with repeatability was found to be 0.8842, and the variance associated with reproducibility was found to be 0.2466. What is the total process variance?
content.why: Total variability includes the part-to-part variability in addition to gage/measurement variability: σ²Total = σ²Gage + σ²p = σ²Reproducibility + σ²Repeatability + σ²p, where σ²p is part-to-part variability. Since part-to-part variability isn't given here, there isn't enough information to determine the total variability. [IV.F]

content.stem: In an acceptance sampling plan, how does the probability of acceptance change for a given fraction nonconforming as the acceptance number increases? Assume that the sample size and lot size are held constant.
content.why: As the acceptance number c increases (with sample size and lot size held constant), the probability of acceptance increases for a given fraction nonconforming: for example, with n=15 and p=0.10, Pa rises from 0.2059 at c=0 to 0.9444 at c=3. [IV.C.1]

content.stem: A manufacturer produces a particular part that is complex. Which of the following measurement tools is most appropriate to inspect its dimensions?
content.why: Coordinate measuring machines are used for dimensional quality control for complex parts. They allow measurements to be completed within minutes. Precision spindles are used to make roundness measurements, micrometer calipers are used to take linear measurements, and go/no-go gages are used to assess specification conformance. [IV.D.1]

content.stem: Type II error in hypothesis testing corresponds to which of the following in acceptance sampling?
content.why: A type II error in hypothesis testing is the probability of failing to reject the null hypothesis when in fact the null hypothesis is false. This corresponds to the consumer’s risk in acceptance sampling: the probability of accepting a lot that does not meet the lot tolerance percent defective (LTPD) level. [IV.C.1]

content.stem: To get more accurate measurements, which of the following surfaces is recommended?
content.why: A granite surface plate provides better hardness compared to iron surface plates and other surfaces. In addition, granite surface plates are more resistant to corrosion and are less responsive to changes in temperature than iron surface plates. [IV.D.1]

content.stem: A manufacturer would like to detect surface defects in a particular part. The surface of this part is made of aluminum. Which of the following testing methods is most appropriate?
content.why: Because the surface of the part is made of aluminum (a nonmagnetic material), liquid penetration testing is most appropriate to detect surface defects. Note that magnetic particle testing cannot be used because aluminum is a nonmagnetic material. [IV.D.2]

content.stem: The calibration of a measuring standard for a machine has become faulty. This is an example of:
content.why: Errors in measurement are classified as random errors (accidental fluctuations that cannot be predicted) or systematic errors (for example, operator error, calibration error). Faulty calibration is classified as systematic error. [IV.E]

content.stem: A specification is given as 10+0.002/–0.000. The limits for this specification are:
content.why: This is a unilateral tolerance with variation in only one direction. [III.C]

options: Its definition has been changed several times by the International Bureau of Weights and Measures.
Its definition is based on the speed of light.
Its definition is in terms of a physical artifact.
It is the oldest base unit.
content.stem: In what way does the official definition of the base unit of mass differ from the definitions of other base units?
content.why: The kilogram, the base unit of mass, is the only base SI unit still defined in terms of a physical artifact (a platinum-iridium cylinder held at the International Bureau of Weights and Measures); the meter's definition, by contrast, has changed several times and is now based on the speed of light. [IV.E]

options: There is evidence of nonlinearity in this measurement system.
There is evidence of stability issues in this measurement system.
The measurement system is not reproducible.
The measurement system is not repeatable.
content.stem: A certain part has a target length of 5.00 cm. The length of the same type of part was repeatedly measured ten times at three points in time over a two- month period. On day one, the observed average was 5.007; after one month, the observed average was 4.975; after two months, the observed average was 4.824. Which of the following statements is true?
content.why: Bias = Observed average - Reference value at each time point: Day 1 bias = 5.007-5.00 = 0.007; 1 month bias = 4.975-5.00 = -0.025; 2 months bias = 4.824-5.00 = -0.176. Stability measures how well a measurement system performs over time; since bias worsens as time elapses, this indicates instability in the measurement system. [IV.F]

options: Can the design be sufficiently tested?
Is the failure rate acceptably low?
Can the product be shipped without damage?
Can the parts needed for the design be obtained at an acceptable cost?
content.stem: For each design review conducted, there are many different points of view from which the design should be considered. One of these viewpoints is from a reliability standpoint. Which of the following would be a question from a reliability viewpoint?
content.why: Reliability includes metrics such as failure rates for the design under consideration. [III.B.3]

content.stem: A lot size of 50,000 is to be inspected using ANSI/ASQ Z1.4-2003 (R2018). The AQL is 1.0%. What are the required sample size, acceptance number, and rejection number for a single sampling plan (normal, level II inspection)?
content.why: For a lot size of 50,000, the code letter for normal, level II inspection is N; using ANSI/ASQ Z1.4-2003 (R2018) Table II-A at AQL 1.0%, the required sample size is n=500, with acceptance number Ac=10 and rejection number Re=11. [IV.C.2]

options: Accept the lot, since the number of defective items is less than the Re value.
Reject the lot, since the number of defective items is more than the Ac value.
content.stem: The attribute sampling plan for a specific product utilizes an accept value of 3 and reject value of 7. The inspector discovers six defective items in the current sample. What is the next appropriate action?
content.why: In a double-sampling plan, after the first sample the lot is accepted if defects d ≤ Ac, rejected if d ≥ Re, or another sample is drawn if Ac < d < Re. Here d=6, and Ac(3) < 6 < Re(7), so another sample must be drawn. [IV.C.2]

content.stem: A double sampling plan is implemented with the following parameters: n = 75, ac = 2, re = 5, n = 75, ac = 4, re = 7. What is the probability that a decision is 1 1 2 2 2 made (accept or reject the lot) on the first sample if the percent nonconforming p = 0.015?

options: the cost of inspection is high.
the fraction of nonconforming products is high.
inspection of products causes inspector fatigue.
content.stem: 100% inspection is most appropriate when:
content.why: 100% inspection is most appropriate when the fraction of nonconforming products is high; under acceptance sampling most lots would be rejected anyway, and any accepted lots would only be accepted due to sampling variability. [IV.C.1]

options: provide information on how well a process is operating.
are generally less expensive to implement.
can monitor multiple quality characteristics at once.
are easier to administer in practice.
content.stem: When compared with attributes sampling plans, variables sampling plans:
content.why: Variables sampling plans use the actual measurements of the product of interest. Therefore, these sampling plans determine how close the process is performing relative to specification limits. Attributes sampling plans only tell us whether to accept or reject a lot and do not provide any additional information about the process. [IV.C.2]

options: The failure of one subsystem results in the failure of the entire system.
They have higher reliability than parallel systems.
More than one subsystem must fail for the system to fail.
They are more complex than parallel systems.
content.stem: Which of the following is a characteristic of series systems?
content.why: A series system is made up of n components connected end to end. Therefore, if one component fails, the entire system fails. [III.E.2]

content.stem: In the third region identified in a bathtub curve, what are the most common type of failures?
content.why: The third region of a bathtub curve is the wear-out region, where there is an increasing failure rate over time. Components that rotate or have alternating motions frequently wear out over time. [III.E.3]

content.stem: A component in a car failed three times out of 1,000 trials during testing (a 0.3% occurrence rate). If this component fails, the only consequence is that the car fails to cold-start. A risk matrix cross-tabulates occurrence rate (0.1%-1%, 1.1%-5%, 5%-10%) against three severity levels: cold-start failure, loss of speed during drive, and total loss of power during drive. At the lowest occurrence band (0.1%-1%), all three severity levels read Low, Medium, and High respectively for cold-start failure, loss of speed, and total loss of power. According to this risk matrix, what is the risk level of this failure?
content.why: For an occurrence rate of 0.3% (3 failures in 1,000 trials), which falls in the 0.1%-1% occurrence band, and cold-start-failure severity, the risk matrix gives Low. [VII.B.2]

content.stem: What is the maximum possible value of an RPN calculated using three 1–10 rating scales?
content.why: The risk priority number (RPN) is determined by multiplying the three components of risk together: severity, occurrence, and detection. Each of these components is given a score on a 1 to 10 scale. Therefore, the maximum possible value of RPN is 10 × 10 × 10 = 1,000. [III.E.4]

content.stem: Consider the product/process development life cycle. The phase in which a working model of the product or process is developed and tested is referred to as the:
content.why: In the prototype phase, a working model is created and tested. One goal is to determine whether the product/process will perform as intended. [III.B.1]

content.stem: A specification is given as 8+0.05/–0.05. The limits for this specification are:
content.why: This is a bilateral tolerance with allowable variation in both directions. [III.C]

content.stem: A new app released for cell phones occasionally slows functionality during customer use. How would the app’s developing company classify this defect?
content.why: An app that occasionally slows functionality during use would not cause an injury or result in a large economic loss. Therefore, this would be classified as a minor defect. [IV.B.3]

content.stem: The failure rate of a machine is 0.0008. Assuming the life distribution of this type of machine is exponential, what is the probability that a randomly selected machine will fail by the mean time to failure (MTTF)?
The mean time to failure (MTTF) for a machine is 525 hours. What fraction of machines fail by 1000 hours? Assume the reliability of the machine has an exponential distribution.
content.why: One interpretation of the failure function F(t) is the fraction of all units in the population that fail by time t. Since MTTF = 525, λ = =1/525. MTTF Therefore, F(1000)=1−R(1000)=1−e−λ(1000) =1−e − 525 =1−0.1489= 0.8511. Approximately 85% of the population will fail by 1,000 hours. [III.E.2]

options: It is a measure of the instantaneous rate of failure of a component at time t.
It is the probability that a component will survive past time t.
It is the fraction of all components in the population that survive past time t.
It is the average number of failures through time t.
content.stem: Which of the following statements best describes the hazard rate function h(t)?
content.why: The hazard function h(t) = f(t)/R(t) = (number of failures per unit time) / (number of components still surviving per unit time), so it represents the instantaneous rate of failure at a given time t. [III.E.1]

content.stem: What are the components of risk as assessed in an failure mode and effects analysis (FMEA)?
content.why: The risk associated with each potential failure mode is assigned a risk priority number (RPN). The RPN is made up of three components: severity, occurrence, and detection. [III.E.4]

content.stem: What is the effect of a factor that is indistinguishable from the effect of the interaction of two other factors called?
content.why: Confounding occurs when the effect of one factor is indistinguishable from the effect of another factor or factor interactions. An interaction is the change in response when two or more factors are interdependent. Randomization is the ordering of treatment combinations in a random sequence to reduce the effect of nuisance variables on the response. Efficiency in experimental design refers to an experiment that generates the maximum information while using a small number of runs and resources. [VI.H.3]

content.stem: A company is releasing a new computer and is developing a flowchart that will include a list of the critical parts in the computer, each part’s vendor, and detailed shipping records. The flowchart is an example of:
content.why: A material flow or traceability flowchart should include the critical components and their part numbers, a list of vendors for each component, information on any internally manufactured parts (including manufacture date), and detailed, computerized shipping records. [IV.B.1]

content.stem: A machine has three identical and independent subsystems, each with a reliability of 0.95. The system design requires that a minimum of two subsystems must function for the system to operate. What is the system reliability of this machine?
content.why: This is a k-out-of-n system with k=2, n=3, p=0.95. Summing the binomial terms for 2 and 3 subsystems surviving: Rs(t) = C(3,2)(0.95)²(0.05)¹ + C(3,3)(0.95)³(0.05)⁰ = 0.1354 + 0.8574 = 0.9928. [III.E.2]

options: To develop a quality process output
content.stem: Which of the following is a reason for identifying Critical to Qualities?
content.why: Critical to Qualities are useful for the development of a quality process output. [III.B.1]

content.stem: Suppose an experiment has four factors A, B, C, and D, with four, two, three, and two levels investigated, respectively. How many treatment combinations are in a full-factorial experimental design for these factors?
content.why: A full-factorial design carries out all treatment combinations of the factors: 4×2×3×2 = 48. [VI.H.1]

content.stem: SWOT is the acronym for:
content.why: SWOT analysis (strengths, weaknesses, opportunities, and threats) is conducted to assess strengths and weaknesses of an organization, to predict opportunities, and to identify threats from competitors. [I.B.1]

content.stem: Which of the following involves demonstrating that all equipment being used in a process has been installed properly (as per manufacturer’s specifications)?
content.why: Installation qualification ensures that all equipment involved is installed properly per manufacturer's specifications. [III.D]

content.stem: Twenty-eight failures occurred after 750 machines were tested for five hours. What is the MTTF for these machines, assuming the reliability of this machine has an exponential distribution?
content.why: The failure rate λ = failures / total test time = 28/(750×5) = 0.0075. MTTF = 1/λ ≈ 133, assuming an exponential life distribution. [III.E.2]

content.stem: A certain computer company will not build their final product until a customer supplies them with all their desired options. What type of system does this company use?
content.why: A pull system is emphasized in a lean enterprise. In a pull system, an action will initiate the next step in the process occurring. In this case, the customer’s order initiates the completion of the computer. Using a pull system eases the burden of making accurate forecasts of customer demand and helps to reduce unused inventory. [V.D]

content.stem: The failure rate of a machine is 0.0008. Assuming the life distribution of this type of repairable machine is exponential and the MTTR is forty-eight hours, what is the steady-state availability of this machine?
content.why: With λ=0.0008, MTBF = 1/λ = 1,250 hours. With MTTR=48 hours, steady-state availability A = MTBF/(MTBF+MTTR) = 1250/1298 = 0.9630. [III.E.2]

content.stem: What is the recommended first step to take when prioritizing corrective action when many FMEA RPNs are clustered?
content.why: Note that ranking RPNs works effectively to prioritize corrective action when there is “comfortable” separation between the RPN values. When these values are clustered, the recommended strategy is to eliminate the occurrence to reorder the RPNs, then reduce the severity, reduce the occurrence, and improve detection. [III.E.4]

content.stem: Which of the following terms describes the phenomenon in which high-order interactions are negligible and a system is dominated by the main effects and low-order interactions?
content.why: The sparsity-of-effects principle is an assumption that is often made that higher-order interactions (orders higher than two-factor interactions) do not have a large effect on the response. This principle is useful when full-factorial designs are conducted with only one replicate. [VI.H.4]

options: The probability that a random lawn mower will survive for a time less than t is 4,890/5,000.
4,890/5,000 of all lawn mowers in the population fail by time t.
The probability that a randomly selected lawn mower fails by time t is 4,890/5,000.
The probability that a randomly selected lawn mower will survive for a time greater than t is 4,890/5,000.
content.stem: The reliability function at time t for a lawn mower is R(t) = 4,890/5,000. Which of the following statements is true?
content.why: The reliability function is defined as the fraction of all components that have survived for a time greater than t. Therefore, the probability that a randomly selected lawn mower will survive longer than t is 4890/5000. Note that the cdf of the failure time [F(t) = 1 – R(t)] can be interpreted as the probability that a randomly selected unit fails by time t or is the fraction of all units in the population that fail by time t. [III.E.1]

content.stem: Which of the following graphical tools can be used to find the optimal settings of factors in a factorial experiment?
content.why: A contour plot of the fitted model can help find optimal settings of factors. A contour plot displays the predicted response over the range of the significant factors. Note that main effects plots and interaction plots can also provide useful information in selecting optimal settings of factors. [VI.H.4] –

content.stem: Which of the following probability distributions is often used to model the first region of the general failure rate model (the bathtub curve)?
content.why: The first region of the bathtub curve is known as the “early life” region and is characterized by a decreasing failure rate function. Since the failure rate is time- dependent in this region, the Weibull distribution is frequently used to model this region of the bathtub curve. [III.E.3]

content.stem: Consider a system with three components arranged in parallel, each labeled with its reliability within its box: 0.99, 0.92, and 0.95. What is the reliability of the overall system?
content.why: The diagram shows a parallel system with three components. Parallel-system reliability is Rs(t) = 1 - [(1-0.99)(1-0.92)(1-0.95)] = 1 - [0.01×0.08×0.05] = 1 - 0.00004 = 0.99996. [III.E.2]

options: it is more difficult to analyze.
content.stem: A disadvantage of using a fractional factorial experiment is that:
content.why: A fractional factorial experiment uses fewer runs; however, not all interactions of interest may be estimable separately from main effects or other interactions. Some of the effects may be confounded with other effects. This can make it difficult to identify which factor or interaction is significant. [VI.H.5]

content.stem: For a process, confirming that specified requirements have been fulfilled is known as:
content.why: Verification deals with determining whether the product or process satisfies specified requirements — it meets all specifications. This does not guarantee the product works as intended. [III.D]

content.stem: A preventive maintenance policy is recommended when the failure rate is:
content.why: If the failure rate is decreasing, constant (such as when the reliability of the system has an exponential distribution), or unknown, maintaining the system in an attempt to prevent failures will not affect the probability that the system will fail in the next instant. Therefore, a preventive maintenance policy is not recommended. [III.E.2]

content.stem: The MTTF for a model of dishwasher is 115 months. What is the probability of a given dishwasher failing by 115 months of operation? Assume the reliability of the dishwasher has an exponential distribution.
content.why: With MTTF=115, λ=1/115. Since reliability is exponential, F(115) = 1-R(115) = 1-e^-115/115 = 1-e^-1 = 1-0.3679 = 0.6321. [III.E.2]

options: does not take much time or cost to implement.
must be used with other quality programs such as Six Sigma.
helps identify failures before they occur.
content.stem: A benefit of implementing an FMEA is that it:
content.why: The main benefit of an FMEA is that it helps teams to identify and eliminate/ reduce the negative effects of potential failures before they occur. However, FMEA is expensive. Note that FMEA can be used as a stand-alone tool and does not need to be part of a larger quality system such as Six Sigma. [III.E.4]

options: Increasing the cost of the experiment
content.stem: A team decided to change the range of temperature from 150–250°F to 175–225°F in an experimental design. What is a potential disadvantage of changing the range of this factor?
content.why: Selecting the range of factors in an experimental design is extremely important. In this problem, the range of the factor has been decreased. If the range of factors is too narrow, it is possible to miss important effects. [VI.H.2]

content.stem: Regulatory requirements, customer needs, and product capabilities are examples of:
content.why: Regulatory requirements, customer needs, product or process capability, and product reliability are some of the inputs that will place requirements on the design. [III.B.3]

options: a specification for achieving high quality.
what is needed to achieve what the customer asks for.
a clearly stated need of the customer.
content.stem: A driver in a Critical to Quality Tree is:
content.why: The driver in a Critical to Quality Tree is what is needed to achieve what the customer asks for and will have lower-level Critical to Qualities that define what is needed to accomplish the driver. [III.B.1]

content.stem: In a test of a component of a machine, 350 components were tested for eight hours and sixty-two components failed. If the mean time to repair these components is three hours, what is the steady-state availability of this component?
content.why: λ = failures/total test time = 62/(350×8) = 0.0221, so MTBF = 1/λ ≈ 45.25 hours. With MTTR=3 hours, availability A = MTBF/(MTBF+MTTR) = 45.25/48.25 ≈ 0.9378. [III.E.2]

options: The uniform distribution is a good reliability model.
content.stem: Which of the following statements is true regarding the second region of the bathtub curve?
content.why: The second region of the bathtub curve is the constant failure rate region. Since failures occur randomly over time in this region, the failure rate is constant. The exponential distribution is frequently used to model the reliability in this region. [III.E.3]

content.stem: In a resolution IV fractional factorial experiment, two-factor interactions are confounded with:
content.why: Resolution IV designs have main effects confounded with three-factor or higher interactions, and two-factor interactions confounded with two-factor or higher interactions. With a resolution IV design, it is unknown for sure that a two-factor interaction is truly significant or whether the two-factor interaction it is aliased with is significant. Additional experimental runs may be needed to break these aliases. [VI.H.5]

content.stem: Consider an experiment with seven factors each at two levels. The complete defining relation is I = ABCDF = ABDEG = CEFG. What resolution is this design?
content.why: A design's resolution equals the length of the shortest word in its defining relation; since the shortest word here (ABCDF, ABDEG, CEFG) is four characters, this is a resolution IV design. [VI.H.5]

options: after completion of the product, process, or service.
content.stem: Validation of a product, process, or service is normally carried out:
content.why: Validation takes place after the product, process, or service is finished or completed. Validation is used to determine whether predetermined requirements are being met (product/process/service is working as intended). [III.D]

content.stem: What fraction of all rechargeable batteries fail by ten hours if the MTBF is eight hours? Assume the reliability of these batteries has an exponential distribution.
content.why: With MTBF=8, λ=1/8. F(10) = 1-R(10) = 1-e^-10/8 = 1-0.2865 = 0.7135, so about 71% of batteries fail by ten hours. [III.E.2]

content.stem: Gale and Wood (1994) introduced seven tools of customer value analysis. They described different perspectives on what customers believe is of value in a product or service. Which of the following would often be considered a value by the customer?
content.why: Staying with the original perspective experts and customers have when it comes to value (a positive outcome in this case), then quality would be the correct answer. [I.G]

None of the main effects or interactions

Assuming the normality and variance assumptions are valid, which terms have a significant effect on the response variable? Source df SS MS F p-value A 1 16.0 16.0 3.20 0.1114 B 1 12.0 12.0 2.40 0.1599 C 1 5.0 5.0 1.00 0.3466 AB 1 2.5 2.5 0.50 0.4996 AC 1 1.5 1.5 0.30 0.5988 BC 1 0.5 0.5 0.10 0.7599 ABC 1 0.25 0.25 0.05 0.8287 Error 8 40.0 5.0 Total 15
content.why: From the ANOVA table, none of the factors in this experiment has a significant effect on the response. The p-values for all main effects and interaction terms are relatively large (> 0.10); therefore, the conclusion is that none of the factors significantly affect the response. [VI.H.4]

content.stem: A tool is designed so that, upon assembly, a component can be attached to the tool in only one position. What type of prevention action does this describe?
content.why: This is an example of a fail-safe device: since the component can only be attached in one position, the tool has been error-proofed against incorrect assembly. [V.F]

content.stem: Consider a system with three components arranged in series, each labeled with its reliability within its box: 0.99, 0.92, and 0.95. What is the reliability of the overall system?
content.why: The diagram shows a series system with three components. Series-system reliability is the product of the component reliabilities: Rs(t) = 0.99 × 0.92 × 0.95 = 0.8653. [III.E.2]

content.stem: Consider the control frame below. L 0.01 A B C “B” represents:
content.why: B represents the secondary datum. [III.C]

content.stem: An advantage of a corrective maintenance policy is that it:
content.why: While a corrective maintenance policy allows for the maximum run time between repairs, it is not the most efficient or cost-effective. If there is a catastrophic failure, the repair time may be extensive, with high costs. [III.E.2]

content.stem: A machine has six subsystems and will fail when four or more of these subsystems fail. What type of system design does this machine have?
content.why: A k-out-of-n system design requires that a system made up of n subsystems must have a minimum of k subsystems functioning to operate. In this case, since the machine will fail if four of six subsystems fail, the machine has a 3-out-of-6 system design, since at most three subsystems can fail before the machine fails. [III.E.2].

content.stem: An experiment has eight factors at two levels each. The experiment has sixty-four runs. What is the experimental design called?
content.why: The experiment has 2^8-2 = 64 runs, making this a one-fourth-fractional factorial design. [VI.H.5]

options: the likelihood of a failure occurring.
the consequences of a failure mode and its frequency of occurrence.
the likelihood of detecting a failure once it has occurred.
the severity of a failure if it occurs.
content.stem: Criticality measures
content.why: Criticality is an assessment of the consequences of a failure mode along with how frequently it occurs. [III.E.4]

options: At the time of its release
content.stem: When can the reliability of a product be measured?
content.why: Reliability cannot be measured at any time prior to the release of the product; it can only be predicted. This is because the reliability of a product is dependent on many factors, including the system design, the reliability of its components, the operating environment, environmental factors, and manufacturing defects. [III.E.1]

content.stem: Which of the following is considered attribute data?
content.why: Attribute data describes discrete data in quality control. Wait time, processing cost, and thickness are all continuous measurements, but the number of filing errors can only take a countable set of values, making it discrete (attribute) data. [VI.A.1]

content.stem: A population has a distribution with mean 24 and standard deviation 5.5. What is the approximate standard deviation of the sampling distribution of the sample mean if random samples of size 32 are taken?
content.why: By the central limit theorem, the sampling distribution of X̄ has standard deviation σX̄ = σ/√n. Here σ=5.5, n=32, so σX̄ = 5.5/√32. [VI.C.2]

options: Attempt to fix the problem on their own.
Follow the reaction plan detailed in the control plan of the process.
Brainstorm to determine the cause of the problem.
Nothing; the process will stabilize on its own.
content.stem: A control chart monitoring the viscosity of a product shows that a particular process is out of control. What should the process operator do?
content.why: Control plans include detailed reaction plans to follow when the control method detects a problem; the reaction plan details the steps an operator should take when the process has a problem. [IV.A]

options: both the average and range were within the control limits.
neither the average nor range were within the control limits.
only the average was outside the control limits.
only the range was outside the control limits.
content.stem: A control chart for an operation using twenty-five samples of four pieces each found X̄=26.75 and R̄=8.10. During production, a new sample of four pieces measured 20, 29, 40, and 25. At the time this sample was taken, were both the average and range within the control limits?
content.why: A control chart for an operation using twenty-five samples of four pieces each found X̄=26.75 and R̄=8.10. During production, a new sample of four pieces measured 20, 29, 40, and 25. At the time this sample was taken, were both the average and range within the control limits?

options: Reject H₀; conclude that the two means are not statistically significantly different.
Reject H₀; conclude that the two means are statistically significantly different.
Do not reject H₀; conclude that the two means are not statistically significantly different.
Do not reject H₀; conclude that the two means are statistically significantly different.
content.stem: Suppose that the p-value of a hypothesis test on µ₁ − µ₂ is 0.23. What conclusions can be made (use significance level of 10%)?
content.why: With α = 0.10 and p-value = 0.23: since p-value > α, H₀ is not rejected. The conclusion is that the two means are not statistically significantly different. [VI.D.2]

options: The normal distribution is not a reasonable model for the time to failure.
The Weibull distribution is a reasonable model for the time to failure.
The normal distribution is a reasonable model for the time to failure.
Not enough information is provided to draw conclusions.
content.stem: A team measured the time to failure of twenty components and plotted the data on a Weibull probability plot. The plotted points fall approximately along a straight line. What conclusions can be drawn from this plot?
content.why: On a Weibull probability plot, the data are plotted against percentiles based on the Weibull distribution. Since the plotted points fall along a straight line, the Weibull distribution is a reasonable model for the time to failure. [VI.A.7]

content.stem: A team investigated the number of patient falls in a hospital. Fifty-six patients were randomly selected. Out of the fifty-six patients, there were six recorded patient falls. Using this information, construct a 90% confidence interval on the true proportion of patient falls in this hospital.
content.why: With x=6 successes out of n=56, the sample proportion p̂=0.1071. For a 90% CI, zα/2=1.645: p̂ ± zα/2√[p̂(1-p̂)/n] gives 0.0391 ≤ p ≤ 0.1751. [VI.D.1]

content.stem: Find the probability that Z, the standard normal distribution, lies between –1.02 and 0.58.
The date of a customer’s visit to a store is on which measurement scale?
content.why: A date is on an interval scale: there are meaningful differences between two dates (you can subtract them to get the number of days between), but there is no absolute zero, so dates cannot be meaningfully multiplied or divided. [VI.A.2]

content.stem: A control chart was out of control, but the operator failed to adjust the process. What is this called?
content.why: Undercontrol (underadjustment) occurs when a control chart signals out-of-control behavior but the process operator fails to respond and adjust the process. [VI.F.2]

options: The probability that a randomly selected air conditioner fails by time t is 4,996/5,000.
The probability that a randomly selected air conditioner will instantly fail is 4,996/5,000.
The fraction of all units in the lot of air conditioners that fail by time t is 4/5,000.
The probability that a randomly selected air conditioner will instantly fail is 4/5,000.
content.stem: The cumulative distribution function of failure at time t for a type of air conditioner is defined as F(t) = 4/5,000. Which of the following statements is (are) true?
content.why: The cumulative distribution function F(t) gives the probability that a randomly selected unit fails by time t, equivalently the fraction of the population that has failed by time t. Therefore, 4/5,000 is the fraction that fails by time t. The instantaneous failure rate is described by the hazard function, not the cumulative distribution function. [III.E.1]

options: three independent variables and five replicates.
five independent variables and three response variables.
content.stem: A 3⁵ experiment means that there are:
content.why: This notation indicates five independent factors, each run at three levels, for a total of 3^5=243 treatment combinations; it gives no information about the number of responses or replicates. [VI.H.1]

options: The wait times at store A are more variable than those at store B.
The distribution of wait times at both stores is not bell shaped.
The wait times at store B are more variable than those at store A.
Customers at store A tend to wait longer than those at store B.
content.stem: Side-by-side box plots show the wait times of customers at two grocery stores. The box for Store A is much narrower (tighter) than the box for Store B, and both distributions appear approximately symmetric. What can be said about these wait times?
content.why: The box plot for Store A is much tighter than Store B's, indicating more variability in wait times at Store B; both distributions are approximately symmetric. [VI.A.7]

options: High levels of factor B tend to have smaller response values.
There is not an interaction effect between factors A and B.
There is an interaction effect between factors A and B.
Factors A and B do not have an effect on the response variable.
content.stem: A two-way ANOVA was used to test the effects of two factors, A and B, on a response variable. An interaction plot shows that the response changes quite differently across the levels of factor A depending on which level of factor B is used (the lines are not parallel). What conclusions can be drawn from this interaction plot?
content.why: The interaction plot shows the response changing quite differently across levels of factor A depending on the level of factor B, indicating a significant interaction effect between factors A and B. [VI.D.5]

content.stem: Tensile strength of cement is of interest to a company. Historical studies indicate that tensile strength is normally distributed and that the standard deviation of tensile strength is 1.25 psi. A random sample of fifteen cement pieces had a mean tensile strength of 124 psi. The company would like to determine if the mean tensile strength is more than 120 psi at the 5% significance level. What is the test statistic for this hypothesis test?
content.why: For H0: μ=120 vs Ha: μ>120 with known σ, z0 = (124-120)/(1.25/√15) = 12.39, which exceeds the critical value z0.05=1.645, so H0 is rejected: the mean tensile strength is more than 120 psi. [VI.D.2]

options: Fit a linear regression model of the two variables.
Graph the data in a scatter diagram.
Compare histograms of the two variables.
content.stem: A team suspects that there is a linear relationship between two continuous variables. What is the first thing they should do when examining the relationship between these two variables?
content.why: Before calculating statistics or fitting a regression model, the team should first plot the data in a scatter diagram, which reveals whether a relationship between the two variables exists. [V.A]

content.stem: If the probability that event A occurs is 0.62, the probability that event B occurs is 0.09, and events A and B are statistically independent, what is the probability that event A and B both occur?
content.why: Since A and B are statistically independent, P(A∩B) = P(A)P(B) = (0.62)(0.09) = 0.0558. [VI.B.3]

content.stem: A normally distributed process has specifications 20.35 ± 3.50. X and R control charts (based on samples of size four) indicate there is an out-of-control point. The control charts also indicate that X = 20.98 and R = 1.96. What is the process capability?
content.why: The control chart indicated an out-of-control point, meaning the process is not stable (special cause variation is present). Since capability indices assume a stable process, the capability here is unknown. [VI.G.2, VI.G.3]

content.stem: A scatterplot displays the relationship between two variables: as x increases, y clearly tends to decrease, though the points are only moderately clustered around the trend. What is the correlation coefficient of these two variables?
content.why: The scatterplot shows y decreasing as x increases (a negative relationship), and the points aren't tightly clustered, indicating a moderately strong negative correlation of -0.90. [VI.E.2]

content.stem: A team would like to estimate the true average tensile strength of cement. They would like to obtain an estimate within 0.05 MPa of the true average tensile strength with 99% confidence. Based on prior information, it is assumed that σ = 0.50 MPa. What sample size is required to meet these requirements?
content.why: With margin of error E=0.05, σ=0.50, α=0.01, zα/2=2.576: n ≥ (σ·zα/2/E)² = (0.50×2.576/0.05)² = 663.58, so the minimum sample size needed is n=664. [VI.D.1]

options: the sample was within the control limits.
the sample was outside the control limits.
content.stem: A factory collected data on the number of nonconforming parts to construct an np-chart. Fifteen samples of size 150 were collected. They determined that the average fraction nonconforming was p̄ = 0.045. During production, a sample of 150 parts was taken, of which eighteen were nonconforming. At the time this sample was taken:
content.why: With p̄=0.045, m=15, n=150, the np-chart limits are UCL = np̄+3√[np̄(1-p̄)] = 14.36 and LCL = np̄-3√[np̄(1-p̄)] = 4.21. Since the new sample's x=18 exceeds the UCL, the sample is outside the control limits. [VI.F.5]

content.stem: The cumulative distribution function of failure at time t for a computer model is 0.992. What fraction of this computer model fails by time t?
content.why: The cumulative distribution function (cdf) of failure can be interpreted as the fraction of all units in the population that fail by time t. Since F(t) = 0.992 for this computer model, the fraction of this model that fail by time t is 0.992. [III.E.1]

options: The process is out of control.
The process is operating within the specifications.
The process is operating outside the specifications.
content.stem: Consider a c-chart with UCL = 14.31, c̄ = 6.6, and LCL = 0. Starting at the sixteenth sample, there is a run of eight consecutive points that are all increasing. What conclusions can be drawn from this control chart?
content.why: Starting at the 16th point, there is a run of eight consecutive increasing points. One sensitizing rule for out-of-control behavior is six or more points in a row all increasing or all decreasing, so the process is out of control; a control chart says nothing about whether the process meets specification limits. [VI.F.6]

content.stem: Which of the following probability distributions is symmetric?
content.why: The lognormal, exponential, and chi-square distributions are all right-skewed and take only positive values; the normal distribution is the symmetric one among these choices. [VI.C.1]

content.stem: A team wants to predict a person’s cholesterol based on their weight in pounds. The fitted regression equation is Cholesterol = 135 + 0.28 × Weight. What is the predicted cholesterol of a person who weighs 175 pounds?
content.why: Substituting Weight=175: Cholesterol = 135 + 0.28(175) = 184. [VI.E.1]

options: Reject H ; conclude that the variance equals 4 minutes2.
Reject H ; conclude that the variance is less than 4 minutes2.
Do not reject H ; conclude that the variance equals 4 minutes2.
Do not reject H ; conclude that the variance is less than 4 minutes2.
content.stem: A hypothesis test on the variance of the wait times of customers at a store was conducted. You would like to determine if the variance of the wait time is less than 4 minutes2. A random sample of twenty-two wait times had a variance of 1.75 minutes2. At the 5% significance level, what is your conclusion from this hypothesis test?
content.why: For H0: σ²=4 vs Ha: σ²<4 (left-tailed, α=0.05, n=22): χ2₀ = (n-1)s²/σ² = 21(1.75)/4 = 9.1875, which is less than the critical value χ2(0.95,21)=11.591, so H0 is rejected: there is sufficient evidence the variance is less than 4 minutes². [VI.D.2]

content.stem: Accounting for a 1.5σ shift in the mean of a process, how many defective parts per million are produced for a process operating at 6σ quality?
content.why: A process operating at Six Sigma quality (accounting for the standard 1.5σ shift) produces 3.4 defective parts per million. [V.C]

options: Reject H ; conclude that type of parts produced and time of day are independent.
Reject H ; conclude that type of parts produced and time of day are not independent.
Do not reject H ; conclude that type of parts produced and time of day are independent.
Do not reject H ; conclude that type of parts produced and time of day are not independent.
content.stem: Consider the contingency table below. A hypothesis test for independence is conducted to determine whether the number of nonconforming parts produced is independent of time of day. Conforming parts / Nonconforming parts / Totals -- Day: 82 / 18 / 100; Evening: 75 / 19 / 94; Overnight: 45 / 14 / 59; Totals: 202 / 51 / 253. The value of the test statistic for this hypothesis test is 0.757. At the 10% significance level, what is the conclusion from this hypothesis test?
content.why: A contingency table cross-tabulates conforming/nonconforming parts by time of day (day, evening, overnight shifts), yielding a chi-square test statistic of 0.757 for a test of independence. At the 10% significance level, what is the conclusion from this hypothesis test?

content.stem: A population has a distribution that is highly right-skewed. One hundred samples of size 50 are randomly collected, and the 100 sample means are calculated. What is the approximate distribution of these sample averages?
content.why: By the central limit theorem, the distribution of sample averages tends toward normal for sufficiently large samples (a rule of thumb is n>30 or 40), regardless of the shape of the underlying population. [VI.A.6, VI.C.2]

content.stem: The number of defects on a TV screen is being examined. Thirty-two TV screens are randomly chosen each day over a 22-day period and examined for defects. The average number of defects is c = 5.68. What is the upper control limit for a corresponding c-chart?

The voltage of a power supply is of interest to a team. Voltage is assumed to be normally distributed. The voltages of nine randomly selected observations are: 9.66, 8.25, 12.46, 12.35, 11.52, 8.92, 11.00, 11.12, and 11.13. Find the 99% confidence interval on the population standard deviation of the voltage.

options: The process is out of control.
The process is operating within the specifications.
The process is operating outside the specifications.
content.stem: Consider an X̄ chart of a normally distributed process with UCL = 41.84, X̄̄ = 35.87, and LCL = 29.90. There are nine consecutive points above the centerline, starting with the fourth data point. What conclusions can be drawn from this control chart?
content.why: There are nine consecutive points above the centerline starting at the 4th data point. A sensitizing rule for out-of-control behavior is nine points in a row on the same side of the centerline, so the process is out of control; a control chart says nothing about whether it meets specification limits. [VI.F.6]

content.stem: Which of the following probability distributions is the only one to have a constant failure rate?
content.why: The exponential distribution is the only probability distribution to have a constant failure rate. For an exponential distribution with parameter λ, the hazard rate function h(t) = λ. [III.E.1]

content.stem: The fitted regression equation for two variables x and y is yˆ = –7.5x –19. What is the intercept of this line?
content.why: The intercept is the value of y when x=0, so the intercept is -19. [VI.E.1]

content.stem: If the probability that event A occurs is 0.40, the probability that event B occurs is 0.13, and A and B are mutually exclusive, what is the probability that either A or B occurs?
content.why: Since A and B are mutually exclusive, P(A∩B)=0, so P(A∪B) = P(A)+P(B) = 0.40+0.13 = 0.53. [VI.B.3]

content.stem: A hypothesis test is performed at the 5% significance level. The probability of a type II error of the test is 0.15. What is the power for this hypothesis test?
content.why: Power = 1 - P(Type II error) = 1 - β = 1 - 0.15 = 0.85. [VI.D.2]

content.stem: A scatterplot displays the relationship between two random variables: as x increases, y tends to decrease, but the points are loosely scattered around the trend rather than tightly clustered. What is the correlation coefficient of these two variables?
content.why: The scatterplot shows y tending to decrease as x increases (a negative correlation), but the points aren't tightly clustered, indicating a weak negative correlation of -0.39. [VI.E.2]

content.stem: The waiting times in minutes for eight customers at a bank are: 5, 8, 12, 3, 2, 7, 6, and 5. What is the mode for this sample of waiting times?
content.why: The mode is the value that occurs most often in the sample; in this data set, 5 minutes occurs more often than any other observation. [VI.A.6]

content.stem: The dimension of a component has specifications of 10.80 ± 2.50. The process data are normally distributed with mean 10.45 and standard deviation 1.05. Find the actual capability of this process.
content.why: With USL=13.3, LSL=8.3, μ=10.45, σ=1.05: Cpk = min[(USL-μ)/3σ, (μ-LSL)/3σ] = min(0.90, 0.68) = 0.68, which is less than 1, so the process is not capable. [VI.G.3]

options: Reject H ; conclude that the medication errors occur with the same probability.
Reject H ; conclude that the medication errors do not occur with the same probability.
Do not reject H ; conclude that the medication errors occur with the same probability.
Do not reject H ; conclude that the medication errors do not occur with the same probability.
content.stem: A team at a hospital did a project on medication errors. A random sample of medication errors yielded the following results: Type of error Number of errors Incorrect dose 22 Wrong dose 34 Incorrect form 47 Wrong amount 45 Total 148 The team used a goodness-of-fit test to determine whether the medication errors occur with equal probabilities. The test statistic was 10.757. At the 5% significance level, what is the conclusion from this hypothesis test?
content.why: For H0: p1=p2=p3=p4=0.25 (α=0.05, k=4): expected counts Ei=37 each, χ2₀ = Σ(Oi-Ei)²/Ei = 10.757, which exceeds χ2(0.05,3)=7.815, so H0 is rejected: the medication errors do not occur with equal probability. [VI.D.4]

have a large average run length.
content.stem: If a process is out of control, it is desirable to:
content.why: When a process is out of control, a small average run length is desirable so operators detect and address the change quickly; failing to adjust the process (underadjustment) lets additional variation persist. [VI.F.6]

content.stem: A bottling company’s filling process has a normal distribution with mean 24 oz. and standard deviation 0.05 oz. What is the probability that a sample of nine randomly selected bottles will have an average volume less than 23.96 oz?

options: SPC cannot show whether process variation appears to be random.
SPC cannot determine whether a process is improving.
SPC cannot indicate when a process has nonrandom variation.
SPC cannot indicate what caused out-of-control behavior in a process.
content.stem: Which of the following is outside the normal scope of statistical process control (SPC)?
content.why: SPC can show whether a process's variation is random or nonrandom and can help determine whether a process is improving, but it cannot by itself identify what caused out-of-control behavior -- further investigation is required for that. [VI.F.1]

options: The sample size and frequency of sampling to monitor the painting process
content.stem: An employee works in an area of a facility where tools are painted. Which of the following would this employee find in the control plan for the process of painting tools?
content.why: Control plans typically include the following: a description of the process, any equipment used in the process, reference drawing numbers, the process characteristic that is being controlled, how the process characteristic should be evaluated, the sampling plan, the method of control, and a reaction plan if the process goes out of control. [IV.A]

content.stem: A quantity derived from sample data that describes the distribution is called a:
content.why: A statistic is a quantity derived from sample data used to estimate a population parameter; a critical value, by contrast, is the value a test statistic is compared to in hypothesis testing. [VI.B.1]

content.stem: The probability of correctly rejecting a false null hypothesis is called:
content.why: Power = 1 - β = 1 - P(Type II error), the probability of correctly rejecting a false null hypothesis. Type I error is rejecting a true H0; Type II error is failing to reject a false H0. [VI.D.2]

content.stem: A scatterplot displays the relationship between two random variables, showing no discernible linear pattern between them. What is the correlation coefficient of these two variables?
content.why: The scatterplot shows no linear relationship between the two variables, so the correlation coefficient is 0 (the correlation coefficient can only range from -1 to 1). [VI.E.2]

content.stem: A factory has historically produced defective parts 1% of the time. Samples of fifty independent parts produced in the factory are tested for the presence or absence of a defect. The resulting data (the number of parts that are defective) form which type of distribution?
content.why: The number of defective parts among n=50 independent trials, each with a fixed probability of a defect (0.01) and only two possible outcomes, follows a binomial distribution. [VI.C.2]

content.stem: The diameter of a stainless-steel rod is an important quality characteristic. The rod has specifications 1.50 ± 0.08. Data from the process indicate that the distribution is normally distributed, and X̄ and R charts indicate that the process is stable. The control charts used a sample of size four and found that X̄ = 1.4983 and R̄ = 0.0906. What fraction of steel rods will fall outside the specification limits?
The distribution on which np-charts are based is called:
content.why: p-charts and np-charts are based on the binomial distribution. [VI.F.5]

content.stem: Consider the contingency table below. Conforming parts / Nonconforming parts / Totals -- Day: 94 / 5 / 99; Evening: 87 / 10 / 97; Overnight: 65 / 23 / 88; Totals: 246 / 38 / 284. Given a nonconforming part, what is the probability it was made during the day shift?
content.why: P(Day | Nonconforming) = P(Day ∩ Nonconforming)/P(Nonconforming) = (5/284)/(38/284) = 5/38 ≈ 0.13. [VI.B.3]

content.stem: A random sample of eight pieces of plastic tubing is selected. The inside diameter of the tubing is known to be normally distributed. The inside diameters of the eight pieces of plastic tubing are: 0.183, 0.190, 0.180, 0.189, 0.190, 0.188, 0.186, 0.185. Find the 95% confidence interval for the population mean of the inside diameter of the plastic tubing.

options: The age of the car does not have a significant effect on the cost.
The intercept of the regression equation, β , is equal to 0.
The age of the car has a significant effect on the cost.
The intercept of the regression equation, β , does not equal 0.
content.stem: A study on a random sample of sixteen cars was done to evaluate the relationship of age of the car and its cost. The ANOVA table below displays the results of a regression analysis. At the 5% significance level, what conclusions can be drawn from these results? Source df SS MS F p-value Regression 1 429.68 429.68 52.53 0.000 Error 14 114.55 8.18 Total 15 544.23
content.why: For the regression ANOVA (H0: β1=0 vs Ha: β1≠0), F0=52.53 exceeds the critical value F(0.05,1,14)=4.60 (and the p-value 0.000 < 0.05), so H0 is rejected: there is a statistically significant linear relationship between the age of the car and its cost. [VI.E.1]

content.stem: A team at a factory is monitoring the average number of defects in TV screens. Twenty-eight TV screens are randomly selected each day over a 50-day period. The average number of defects per TV screen was found to be u = 0.214. What is the lower control limit for a corresponding u-chart?
content.why: With ū=0.214, n=28: LCL = ū-3√(ū/n) = 0.214-3√(0.214/28) ≈ -0.048, which by convention is rounded up to 0 since a control limit cannot be negative. [VI.F.5]

options: Detailed methods to contain questionable products
content.stem: Which of the following would you typically find in a reaction plan for a process?
content.why: A reaction plan typically contains four elements: containment, diagnosis, verification, and disposition. The reaction plan should therefore include specific directions for the operators on how to contain products that are suspected of being nonconforming or out of spec. [IV.A]

content.stem: What probability distribution is required for the results of a capability study to be considered valid?
content.why: Capability indices are only valid when the underlying process data follow a normal distribution; a histogram or normal probability plot can be used to check this assumption. [VI.G.1]

content.stem: A histogram shows a distribution with a few extremely large values, pulling its tail out to the right while most of the data cluster at lower values. What shape does this distribution have?
content.why: The histogram shows a few extremely large values pulling the distribution's tail to the right, indicating a right-skewed distribution. [VI.A.6]

content.stem: As the degrees of freedom go to infinity, what distribution does Student’s t-distribution become?
content.why: As degrees of freedom approach infinity, Student's t-distribution converges to the standard normal distribution. [VI.C.1]

options: Reject H ; conclude that the two means are not statistically significantly different.
Reject H ; conclude that the two means are statistically significantly different.
Do not reject H ; conclude that the two means are not statistically significantly different.
Do not reject H ; conclude that the two means are statistically significantly different.
content.stem: Two methods for filling a bottle are being compared at a factory. The two methods have known standard deviations σ = 0.05 oz. and σ = 0.04 oz., 1 2 respectively. A random sample of n = 24 bottles using method 1 and an independent random sample of n = 25 bottles using method 2 are collected. The mean volume using method 1 is 15.95 oz., and the mean volume using method 2 is 16.02 oz. Test the hypothesis that the two methods have different mean volumes (use α = 0.10). What is your conclusion?
content.why: For H0: μ1-μ2=0 vs Ha: μ1-μ2≠0 (α=0.10, two-tailed, zα/2=1.645): z0 = (15.95-16.02)/√(0.05²/24+0.04²/25) = -5.398, which is less than -1.645, so H0 is rejected: there is a significant difference in mean fill volume between the two methods. [VI.D.2]

options: Number of members in the household
content.stem: Which of the following characteristics of a company’s customers is considered continuous data?
content.why: Continuous data can take any value over an interval; age can be measured continuously, while gender and hair color aren't numeric and household size is discrete (whole numbers only). [VI.A.1]

Scatterplot of predicted versus actual values
content.stem: Which of the following graphical methods will assess the assumption of normality in the analysis of a designed experiment?
content.why: A normal probability plot of the residuals assesses the normality assumption; the residuals should fall approximately along a straight line if the assumption holds. [VI.H.4]
